true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently breaks the 4-argument form

`self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the width/height variant is unreachable. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)` (or with opts) now binds `h` to `dimensions` and the opts hash/height to `opts`, producing either a bogus `-resize` argument or a `TypeError` when `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` is evaluated on an Integer. Use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height instead of two same-named methods.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings

`maxSizeKB` was read from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. Sites that configure a smaller limit will let users upload files the server will reject (bad UX, wasted bandwidth), and sites configured above 10MB will see valid uploads blocked client-side. The error message also now always says 10240 kb regardless of the actual configured limit. This looks like leftover debug code (PR description is "Test 1") and should read the setting again.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage dimension and extension-less temp path break animated GIF handling

`downsize` is called with the dimension string `"80%"`. For animated images `OptimizedImage.optimize` would dispatch to the gifsicle path, but (a) that branch only triggers when the source path matches `/\.GIF$/i` and the upload tempfile has no `.gif` extension, so it never triggers, and (b) gifsicle's `--resize-fit` does not accept a percentage (`--scale` is the percentage option), so it would fail if it did. Consequently large animated GIFs are run through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently destroys the animation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsize loop uses a possibly stale `tempfile.size` and converts a file in place while its handle is open

The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` (source == destination) and then re-reads `tempfile.size`. `Tempfile#size` stats the still-open file descriptor; ImageMagick/ImageOptim may replace the file (new inode) rather than truncate it in place, in which case the loop keeps seeing the original size, burns all 5 attempts re-shrinking the image, and then passes a wrong filesize to `Upload.create_for`. Re-open/stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion and pass that size to `create_for`.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of configured max image size

In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch no longer uses `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and instead reports `10 * 1024` kb. The user is therefore told a limit that may have nothing to do with the real configured/web-server limit, which is misleading.

API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB instead of the site setting

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Administrators can no longer restrict the amount of remote data an API upload will pull down; a site configured for e.g. 1MB images now fetches up to 10MB per request (resource/DoS exposure), and sites configured above 10MB silently lose functionality. Derive the cap from the setting.

Downsize loop ignores conversion failure

The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded. `convert_with` returns false (and only logs) when ImageMagick or ImageOptim fails, so on failure the loop spins through all 5 attempts invoking an external process each time with no effect, before creating an upload that will be rejected for size. Break out of the loop when the downsize returns false.

No tests for the new downsize API or auto-downsizing path

The change alters the public signature of `OptimizedImage.optimize`/`downsize` (dimension string instead of width/height), removes `self.dimensions`, and adds a new auto-downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but no specs are added or updated. Existing specs that stub/call `optimize(op, from, to, width, height, opts)` or `dimensions` would break, and the new loop (including the size-reread and failure behaviour) is untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!(...)` is called before validation runs. If `host` is nil — which happens whenever the admin endpoint is posted without a host value (`host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` can assign nil) — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` and use the non-destructive `sub` (the destructive `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place).

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id does not exist (stale admin tab, double-delete, guessed id). `host.destroy` on line 16 and `save_host(nil)` from `update` then raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404/error JSON. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response (or `find`, which raises RecordNotFound and is handled).

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host comparison lowercases the column but not the incoming value

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased column against the raw value extracted from the referer. `URI#host` preserves the case the browser sent (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with any uppercase characters will not match a stored host and the embed request will be rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so embedding silently breaks after upgrade

Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting could contain entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old spec and docs explicitly supported this). The migration inserts those raw strings directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` callback that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value with `URI(referer).host`, which never contains a scheme or path, so every migrated row with a scheme/path will stop matching and embedding will start returning `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme and path) before inserting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped

`spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this makes the fabricators impossible to locate by filename and will confuse every future change to either model's fixtures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped string interpolation into INSERT statement

The host value from the old site setting is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any value containing a single quote (or stray whitespace/CR from splitting on "\n" only) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration; it is also an injection vector from stored data. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert, and strip each entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` site setting row is absent

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings are only persisted when changed from their default, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and even when there is, the join on category *name* may not match). `PG::Result#[]` returns nil for a missing row, so `[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`, aborting the migration and leaving the deployment half-migrated. The same problem exists on line 15 for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup. Both queries need nil guards.

false_positives.candidate:
Host format regex rejects valid hosts that previously worked

`\.[a-z]{2,5}` restricts the TLD to 2–5 characters and requires at least one dot, so hosts such as `blog.technology`, `foo.website`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or an intranet hostname are rejected. The replaced `embeddable_hosts` site setting (a `host_list`) accepted these, so admins migrating from it cannot re-add such hosts through the new UI.

Hosts with a port pass validation but can never match a referer

The validation regex permits an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port and the `before_validation` callback only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:3000` is stored as-is. However `record_for_host` matches against `URI(referer).host`, which never includes the port, so any host saved with a port will never be allowed and embedding from that origin always fails. Either strip the port on save or compare against host+port.

Missing `embeddable_host` params cause a 500

`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises `NoMethodError` if the `embeddable_host` key is absent from the request. The controller should require the parameter (e.g. `params.require(:embeddable_host)`) so a malformed request yields a 400 rather than an exception.

No tests for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints

The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. The new `create`, `update` and `destroy` actions control the embedding whitelist (a security boundary: which external sites may embed the forum) and contain non-trivial logic (category fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, nil-record handling, error rendering), none of which is exercised. The same applies to `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. At minimum add tests that a host can be created/updated/deleted, that validation errors are returned, and that a non-admin is refused.

No uniqueness validation or index on host

Nothing prevents two rows with the same host (possibly pointing at different categories), which makes `record_for_host`'s `.first` result arbitrary and therefore the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. There is also no index on `host`, while `host_allowed?` runs on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?`, which cannot use a plain index. Consider a uniqueness validation plus a unique index on `lower(host)`.

Plural embedded hydration crashes on null and silently produces undefined entries

In the new `*_ids` branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serialized value is `null` rather than an array, and `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` can never fall back to `[]` because `hydrated` is always an array — if the side-loaded collection is missing, the result is an array of `undefined` values while the original `*_ids` key is unconditionally deleted, so the data is lost rather than left intact. The singular branch correctly only deletes the key when a lookup succeeded; the plural branch should behave the same and guard against non-array values.

Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer looks at embeddable hosts at all. This example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic, so the name is misleading and the assertion no longer covers anything related to hosts. Rename or remove it.

`create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and its data

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If this migration is ever re-run (or a table of that name already exists, e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied deploy) all existing rows are silently destroyed. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

`embed: :ids` without `include: true` does not side-load the host records

The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not put an `embeddable_hosts` array in the JSON root. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is missing, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. `embed: :ids, include: true` (side-loading) is required.

`embedding#update` is a no-op that reports success

The `update` action persists nothing — it only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will report success without any change having been made. Either implement the update or remove the route, action and the unused client-side `saveChanges`.

`type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore

`String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) will never match an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS` and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`).

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. the user never visited/read the topic, the row was removed, or the topic was merged/moved), and line 107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` on it. Any such request raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 to a user who just clicked an unsubscribe link in an email. The action needs to handle the nil case (create the record or go through `TopicUser.change`, which upserts).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus notification

The new action writes `notification_level` directly on the record instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (the level stays attributed to the old reason, e.g. `auto_watch_category`) and no `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` message is published, so other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level and auto-tracking logic sees an inconsistent reason id.

No specs for the new unsubscribe action

The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint has no request/controller spec. Untested behaviours that are easy to get wrong and are currently broken or risky: missing `TopicUser` row (raises NoMethodError), the watching/tracking -> regular vs regular/muted -> muted transition, the 301 redirect when the slug is absent or mismatched, and the anonymous-user path. Please add specs covering these.

Route name topicUnsubscribe may not resolve the template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs

The route is registered as `topicUnsubscribe`, while the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (i.e. template name `topic/unsubscribe`) and the view at `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` (name `topic-unsubscribe`). The resolver decamelizes/dasherizes route names, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks for `topic_unsubscribe`/`topic-unsubscribe`; the template and view names are therefore inconsistent with each other, and the unsubscribe page risks rendering blank. Please make the names consistent (e.g. put the template at `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`) or add an explicit `renderTemplate`.

State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a GET with no CSRF protection `unsubscribe` is routed as `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and mutates `TopicUser.notification_level`, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it. Because Rails does not verify CSRF tokens for GET requests, any third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user with e.g. ``, silently muting topics. Link-prefetching/scanning agents that carry the user's session (browser prefetch, some security proxies) can also fire it unintentionally. The mutation should happen on a POST/PUT (or be protected by a signed one-time key, like the existing digest unsubscribe key flow).

Unsubscribe link requires an active session

`:unsubscribe` was added to the `ensure_logged_in` before_filter, so a recipient who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email while not logged in (the common case for mail clients in a different browser/profile) gets a not-logged-in error/login redirect instead of unsubscribing. Email unsubscribe flows in this codebase otherwise use a token (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the new link should either use such a key or at least redirect back to this URL after login.

Unsubscribe page text claims notifications stop even when level is only lowered to regular

`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the server action lowers a watching/tracking user to `regular` (not `muted`) on the first click. At `regular` the user still receives notifications/emails for replies, mentions and quotes, so the message is wrong for the most common case and users will believe they are unsubscribed when they are not. Either mute on the first click or make the text reflect the actual resulting level.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} and will raise for callers that don't pass it

The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` provides no default for it (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` are defaulted). Any `build_email` call that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, breaking email delivery. The need to update `message_builder_spec.rb` to add `unsubscribe_url` demonstrates this. Add a fallback in `MessageBuilder` (e.g. default `unsubscribe_url` to the user preferences URL) so existing/plugin callers keep working.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has a DB side effect, so match statistics are double-counted

`validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`). Validation is not idempotent and is run multiple times per request: `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (line 168) and then `user.save` (line 172), each of which runs the email validator, so a single signup attempt bumps `match_count` twice. Any other code that calls `valid?` on a user will also inflate the counters. The statistics gathering should be moved out of the validator (or made explicitly once-per-attempt).

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case sensitive and not normalized

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw value passed in by the validator against the stored string. Email local parts/domains are commonly entered with different casing (e.g. `Block@SpamFromHome.org`), and the `users.email` column is not guaranteed to be downcased at validation time, so a blocked address can be bypassed just by changing capitalization. Normalize (downcase/strip) both on write and on lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Failed save of match statistics is silently swallowed

`record.save` is used without checking the return value. Because the model also runs presence/uniqueness validations on save, a failure (or a validation error introduced later) silently discards the `match_count`/`last_match_at` update with no log, making the statistics quietly unreliable.

Mutable array declared on the controller class is shared between instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single array on the class prototype; `pushObject` in `createAccount` mutates that shared array. Any second instance of `CreateAccountController` (or the same instance reused across modal open/close) sees another instance's rejected emails, and the state is never reset. Initialize it per instance (e.g. in `init`) instead of as a class-level literal.

No coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic moved into EmailValidator

The `email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` behaviour was removed from `User#email_validator` and re-implemented here (including the `elsif` precedence and the `errors[attribute].blank?` short-circuit that skips the blocked-email check). The new spec only exercises the blocked-email branch, so the relocated domain restriction code and the interaction between the two branches are untested after the refactor.

Server-side email error reason is replaced by generic "invalid" message

When the server rejects an email (blocked address, domain not allowed, already taken, …) the controller pushes the value into `rejectedEmails` and the validation then shows `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. The specific reason returned in `result.errors.email` (including the new `user.email.blocked` string added to server.en.yml) is discarded, so users get a misleading "Email is invalid" message for an address that is syntactically valid. Use the server-supplied error text keyed by email instead of a generic constant.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open used with externally supplied URLs (SSRF / command execution)

`open(url).read` in `import_remote` and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed` use `Kernel#open`, which executes a shell command when the argument starts with `|` and happily fetches `file://` and internal addresses. The feed URL is a per-site setting (a site admin on a multisite install should not be able to run commands on the host), and `import_remote` is also invoked from the Disqus importer with URLs taken from the dump. Use `URI.parse(...).open`/`Net::HTTP` restricted to http(s), with a timeout.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that happens to be a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For `discourseUrl = "http://forum.example.com/"`, an attacker-controlled frame on `http://forum.example.co` passes the check. Compare the origin for exact equality against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` instead, and ignore messages whose `source` is not the created iframe.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise a SyntaxError when the view renders

The closing tag of the if/else block is written as `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The compiled template becomes `... end if <buffer append>`, i.e. the stray `if` starts a new, never-closed conditional, so rendering `embed#best` raises a SyntaxError and every embed request for an already-imported topic returns a 500. Controller specs don't render views, so this is not caught by the added tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without `content` raise NoMethodError and abort the whole poll

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the items are processed in a single `each` loop with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one such item aborts the entire polling run and all remaining items are silently skipped. Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the job.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into inline JavaScript (reflected XSS)

`parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates the *host* of the referer, so an attacker-controlled path/query such as `http://<embeddable_host>/x'+alert(document.cookie)+'` passes validation and breaks out of the string literal, executing arbitrary JS in the Discourse origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`j` and preferably pass only the scheme+host origin (which is all postMessage uses anyway).

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

false_positives.candidate:
"ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options value

`response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` sets a non-standard token. Browsers that don't recognise it are entitled to fall back to denying framing, which would break embedding entirely. The reliable way to permit framing is to delete the header (`response.headers.delete('X-Frame-Options')`), optionally alongside a CSP `frame-ancestors` entry for the embeddable host.

Existing embed with a deleted post crashes the import

When a `TopicEmbed` row already exists, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted or the association pointing at a missing row). The code then calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising NoMethodError inside the retrieval job/feed poll. Guard on `post.blank?` and either recreate the topic or skip.

Loading page is cached for 1 minute while the page reloads every 30 seconds

`discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads after 30s. The browser/proxy will serve the cached loading page for the first reload, so the user waits at least a minute even when the topic was imported quickly. Skip caching (or use a much shorter max-age) on the loading response.

No test renders the embed views; assertions hidden in an `after` hook

The specs never render the views (controller specs don't by default), which is why the syntax error in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%- end if %>`) goes undetected — the only new user-facing templates are completely untested. Additionally, `response.should be_success` and the X-Frame-Options assertion live in an `after` block: hook failures are reported detached from the example and run even when the example already failed, making diagnosis hard. Add a `render_views` request/controller spec for `embed#best` (both the loading and the topic-found paths).

Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently block retrieval of a URL

`$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the throttle key exists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, so that embed URL can never be imported again (the embed page will loop on the loading template indefinitely). Use `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` (or `setex` guarded by existence) instead.

`feed_key` is dead code

`feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:` Redis key but nothing in the class (or anywhere else in the PR) reads or writes it, so there is no conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since handling as the name implies. Either implement the caching it was intended for or remove the method so future readers don't assume polling is throttled.

`force: true` added to an already-released migration can drop an existing table

This migration was already shipped; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that on any database where the migration is re-run (re-seeded schema, repaired schema_migrations, `db:migrate:redo`) the existing `top_topics` table is dropped along with its data instead of failing loudly. The change is also unrelated to the embedding feature in this PR and should be reverted.

`import` mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the argument supplied by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or cache the content (and any frozen string passed in, which would raise) get surprising behaviour, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate multiple "Imported from" footers. Use `contents + ...` / `dup` instead.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. Those are rewritten to `http://embedhost//cdn.example.com/img.png` (the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips the leading slashes), producing broken links and broken images for any feed that uses protocol-relative references. Exclude hrefs/srcs starting with `//` before prefixing.

embed_url limited to 255 characters with a unique index

`t.string :embed_url` creates a varchar(255). Article URLs with query strings/UTM parameters routinely exceed 255 characters, so those imports will fail with a value-too-long error (and the unique index on the column limits how long an indexable value can be). Consider `t.text` with an index on a hash/prefix, or document the limit and truncate/normalise the URL before insert.

raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked`

`cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `i.content` from an arbitrary remote RSS/Atom feed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with this cook method, so anything the feed publisher puts in the item body (`<script>`, event handlers, iframes) is rendered verbatim to every forum visitor — a stored XSS vector. Feed/imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (as `import_remote` does with its tag/attribute whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin maps modern `order` values directly onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group properties

`-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (old 2009 flexbox spec) are 1-based and default to 1, while the modern `order` property is 0-based and defaults to 0. Emitting the same raw `$val` for both means legacy WebKit/Gecko engines see an ordering that is shifted by one relative to modern engines, and `@include order(0)` would emit the invalid `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the mixin should emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties.

Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Header .panel right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, unsupported by the legacy box fallbacks added in the same PR

`.panel` lost `float: right` and now relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `order: 3` to be pushed to the right of `.contents`. Auto margins for free-space distribution are a modern flexbox feature; in the legacy `-webkit-box` / `-moz-box` modes that `flexbox()` deliberately emits as fallbacks, `margin-left: auto` does not consume free space, so in those engines the header panel (user/notifications/search icons) will no longer be right-aligned — it will sit directly after the title. If those fallbacks are meant to be functional, use `-webkit-box-flex`/spacer handling or drop the legacy display values.

Percentage padding on .small-action-desc makes text indentation viewport-dependent

`.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's width, so the horizontal inset now varies with the topic/viewport width instead of being a fixed, font-relative amount; combined with the fact that `.small-action-desc` is a flex item with no `flex` value (so it only takes its content width), the text position and wrapping of small-action messages will be inconsistent across widths. A fixed em/px padding plus `flex: 1` would be more predictable.

`float: right` on .small-action button no longer works now that .small-action is a flex container

`.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264), which makes `float` a no-op on all of its direct children. The `button { ... float: right; }` rule at line 306-310 (used for the small-action action buttons, e.g. undo/delete) will therefore no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` in normal flex order. To keep the button right-aligned, use `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) instead of a float.

align-items() mixin is inconsistent with flexbox() and will emit invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end/stretch

`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for legacy Gecko, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so legacy Gecko gets the old box display with no alignment. Either translate the values inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes.

Only `path` is appended; query/fragment are dropped and `URI()` is re-parsed repeatedly

`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` drops any query string or fragment, so `http://example.com/u?id=1` is displayed as `example.com/u`, which does not match the href the user clicks. It also re-parses the URI on every branch (up to twice per call) outside the `rescue nil` guard of line 138. The second branch considers two hosts related whenever they have the same number of labels (>2) and match after dropping the first label. For shared hosting suffixes this is wrong: with an instance on `forum.github.io`, an arbitrary user website `spammer.github.io` is judged to belong to the same organisation and the full URL path is rendered instead of only the host. The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only contains `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not asserted to be absent, which is why the regression that leaks a TL0 user's website host/path to anonymous visitors is not caught. `"" << website_host` mutates a string literal instead of concatenating

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment the file gets a `# frozen_string_literal: true` magic comment (or runs under `--enable-frozen-string-literal`), breaking user serialization site-wide. Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

`website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking TL0 websites to anonymous users

`:website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous visitors (anti-spam / SEO protection). The new `:website_name` attribute was added to `attributes` but not to `untrusted_attributes` and has no working inclusion guard, so the host (and now even the full path) of a TL0 user's website is serialized for anonymous requests, and `user.hbs` renders it (`{{#if model.website_name}}`). This re-exposes exactly the spam vector the untrusted_attributes list exists to block. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

totalPages off by one produces an extra empty page

`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 150 members with limit 50) this yields 4 instead of 3. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, the "next" arrow stays enabled on the real last page, advancing `offset` to 150 and rendering an empty member list labelled page 4/4. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findMembers returns undefined for unnamed groups instead of a promise

Any caller that chains on the result — e.g. `group.findMembers().then(...)`, or the controller's `next`/`previous` actions whose return value is used by the Ember action/promise machinery — will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. Return a resolved promise instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Breaking change to /groups/:name/members.json response shape and default truncation

The endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized members (and only paginated automatic groups). It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and applies a default `limit` of 50 to every group. Any existing consumer (plugins, mobile clients, scripts) that iterates the top-level array will break, and callers that relied on getting the whole membership now silently receive at most 50 users. This needs at least a changelog/version note, and ideally the pagination default should be documented; consider whether the old array shape must be preserved for compatibility.

Lost coverage for unknown/non-member usernames and no coverage for the new members pagination

The old specs asserted that adding a non-existent username and removing a non-member succeed silently; those cases are dropped here even though `add_members` still swallows unknown usernames, so that behaviour is now untested. Additionally, `GroupsController#members` was rewritten (new `{members:, meta:}` envelope, new default limit, new offset handling) without any spec update, so the response shape and the limit/offset edge cases are entirely uncovered.

Unvalidated limit/offset in public members endpoint

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()` on this unauthenticated-reachable endpoint. A negative value (e.g. `/groups/foo/members.json?offset=-1` or `limit=-1`) makes PostgreSQL raise "OFFSET must not be negative" / "LIMIT must not be negative", turning user input into a 500, and an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `limit=1000000`) forces the server to load and serialize every member of a large group, which is an easy resource-exhaustion vector. Clamp both values (e.g. offset >= 0, limit between 1 and a sane maximum).

addMembers/removeMember ignore server errors

`addMembers` and `removeMember` fire `model.addMembers(...)` / `model.removeMember(...)` without attaching a rejection handler. The server returns 422 for automatic groups and can also fail for other reasons, and unknown usernames are silently skipped by `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`. The admin therefore gets no feedback at all: the input keeps its content (see the "TODO: should clear the input"), the list is not refreshed, and nothing indicates the operation failed. Add a failure handler that surfaces the error message (as the `save` action already does).

add_members raises NoMethodError when usernames is sent as an array

`usernames.split(",")` assumes the parameter is a String. An API client (or a nested form encoding such as `usernames[]=bob`) yields an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, producing an unhandled NoMethodError / 500 instead of a 400-class response. Coerce with `Array(params[:usernames]).join(',').split(',')` or validate the type explicitly.

create silently drops alias_level

`create` only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`, but the client's `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` (used by both `create` and `save`) always sends `alias_level`, and the admin form lets you pick an alias level before the first save. As a result a newly created group is always persisted with the default alias level and the user's selection is lost without any error; it only takes effect if they save a second time (where `update` does honour `alias_level`). `create` should assign `alias_level` the same way `update` does.

remove_member bypasses Group#remove, leaving user_count counter cache and primary_group stale

`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association removes the join rows with a `delete_all`, which skips ActiveRecord callbacks. `GroupUser` maintains `groups.user_count` through a counter cache / callbacks, and `Group#remove` additionally clears `users.primary_group_id` when the removed group was the user's primary group. By deleting the join rows directly, the group's `user_count` column is never decremented (so the admin group list and the new `{{user_count}}`/pagination UI show wrong totals forever) and a removed member can keep the deleted group as their primary group. The symmetric add path correctly uses `group.add(user)`; removal should use `group.remove(user)` (after looking the user up) so the same bookkeeping runs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX

`ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes and reads `@loaded_locales` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two threads can both observe nil and each install a fresh array, so a locale recorded as loaded by one thread can be dropped, and `include?` can be executed concurrently with `<<`/reassignment. On non-GVL runtimes this can corrupt the array or cause repeated/missed loads. Initialize `@loaded_locales` eagerly at patch load time or perform the check inside the mutex.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere

The on-demand locale loader in `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (line 68). The newly added fallback chain is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers/user notifications, rake tasks, rails console, middleware that runs before/without the before_filter — will have only the primary locale's YAML loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up the fallback locales (site default locale and `:en`) in an empty translation store and still produce a missing translation. The fallback feature therefore works inconsistently depending on the execution context. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (i.e. whenever a locale is activated) rather than only in the controller filter.

FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes on every lookup, defeating Hash memoization

`I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation lookup. Unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which memoizes computed chains in the Hash, this override ignores the Hash storage and rebuilds a new array (plus a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a `to_sym`) on each call. On a hot path such as rendering a page with many translations this adds an allocation and a site-setting lookup per translation; consider caching per locale (and invalidating when `default_locale` changes).

No tests for the new fallback behaviour

This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), moves pluralization setup, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, yet no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves from `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then `:en`, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` dedupes, or that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locale files. Given that fallbacks are now active in all environments (the per-environment `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed), regressions here would silently change every missing-translation lookup, including in the test suite where missing translations will now be masked by the :en fallback.

Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain (stale/cross-site translations)

The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is computed per request in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`. Two consequences: (1) after an admin changes `default_locale`, previously cached fallback results for other locales remain in the process-level LRU cache and keep returning values resolved through the old fallback locale until a reload; (2) in a multisite deployment the LRU cache is shared across all sites in the process while `SiteSetting.default_locale` is per-site, so a string resolved through site A's fallback locale can be served to site B for the same locale/key. The cache key needs to include the fallback chain (or the current site/default locale), or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes a FallbackLocaleList and will 500 if fallbacks are replaced

`ensure_loaded!` is defined only on the custom `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. If anything else assigns `I18n.fallbacks` (a plugin, or `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` still present in an environment file such as development.rb/test.rb or a deployment's own copy of production.rb, which installs a plain `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`), this before_filter raises `NoMethodError` on every single request, taking the whole site down. Either define the loading helper in a place that does not depend on the fallbacks object type (e.g. in the translate accelerator, loading `I18n.fallbacks[I18n.locale]`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise, and `.uniq.compact` ordering is wrong

`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` unguarded. If the setting is nil/not yet available (e.g. during asset precompilation, early boot, or before migrations create the site_settings table) this raises `NoMethodError`/DB errors from inside every `I18n.translate` call, since `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` invokes `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each lookup. Also, `compact` is applied after `uniq`, so a nil `locale` argument is only removed after being compared — the intent (drop nils, then dedupe) would be `.compact.uniq`. Guard the setting lookup (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`) and reorder.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation

UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method added in this PR is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and no no-arg overload exists in this class or in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. This does not compile, so the whole services module fails to build. Either add a no-arg overload (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) or pass `context.getUser()` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, inverting the previous behaviour and disabling conditional passkeys on the first login screen

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` was executed exactly when `context.getUser() == null` (authenticate(), old else-branch) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` when the user was not yet selected. With the new helper, both call sites (lines 115 and 137) now do the opposite: the WebAuthn/conditional-UI data is only filled when a user is already set (re-authentication), and is never filled for a plain login where no user has been established yet. Consequently the normal passkeys autofill/conditional-UI on the initial username+password page disappears (no challenge, no rpId, no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI), which breaks the primary passkeys login flow and the existing assertions in these tests that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page. The condition most likely should be `user == null || user has a passwordless WebAuthn credential` rather than `user != null`.

false_positives.candidate:
Broad catch(Exception) around element lookup can make the assertion vacuous

The two `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { }` blocks (lines 291-296 and 312-317) swallow any RuntimeException from WebDriver, not just NoSuchElementException (e.g. StaleElementReferenceException or a WebDriver timeout), so the test can pass without ever proving the webauthn form is absent. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` as done in the other tests in this package.

No test for re-authentication of a passkey-less user while passkeys are enabled for the realm

`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` only sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`, i.e. it verifies the trivial case where passkeys are disabled realm-wide. The behaviour actually changed by this PR is re-authentication with passkeys *enabled* for the realm: in that case `fillContextForm` is now invoked for an already-identified user, and because `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` returns false the previous 'user has no WebAuthn credential' short-circuit no longer applies. There is no test covering a user that has only a password while realm passkeys are enabled, which is exactly the regression-prone path.

Unconditionally returning false removes the guard that skipped the passkey form for users without WebAuthn credentials

`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` is overridden to always return false. In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` this branch also contained the check `if (authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()) return null;`, which prevented rendering passkey UI for an identified user that has no WebAuthn credential. Since the conditional-UI authenticator is now also used while a user is already set (re-authentication), a user who only has a password but belongs to a realm with passkeys enabled will now get the passkey/conditional-UI markup rendered on the re-authentication form (with IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false and no allowCredentials), so any passkey attempt can only fail or, worse, let the browser offer a discoverable credential of a different user which then aborts the flow with WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER. The 'no credentials' case should still suppress the passkey UI.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative queryset slice is not supported by Django and will raise, not "handled automatically"

In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and the client supplies a cursor with a negative offset, `start_offset = cursor.offset` is negative and `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is executed. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indices (`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), so this path can never work: it turns a user-controlled cursor value into an unhandled 500 instead of a `BadPaginationError`/400. The inline comment claiming "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually wrong. Either validate `offset >= 0` and raise `BadPaginationError`, or remove the feature.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`organization_context.member` can be None, raising AttributeError on every request

`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally for every GET on this endpoint, before checking `use_optimized`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is optional and is `None` when the requester is not a member of the organization (e.g. a superuser/staff user, or an org-auth-token/API-key request that passes the `OrganizationAuditPermission` check without membership). Because Python's `or` short-circuits only when the left side is truthy, a non-superuser non-member will dereference `None.has_global_access` and the endpoint will return a 500 instead of the audit log page. Guard with `use_optimized and organization_context.member is not None` (and only compute the flag inside the optimized branch).

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes for datetime sort keys

`get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to `getattr(item, self.key)`. The only caller added in this PR (`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`) uses `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Every request with `?optimized_pagination=true` from an eligible user will 500 as soon as a cursor is built. Either subclass `DateTimePaginator`'s key conversion or do not use this paginator for datetime columns.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
"authorized administrators" gate actually grants the feature to ordinary members

The comment says the optimized path is for "authorized administrators", but the condition uses `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, which is true for any member of an organization with open membership (and for members whose role grants global access) — not just admins. Any such user can set `?optimized_pagination=true` and reach `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which deliberately bypasses the offset lower-bound (see `paginator.py`). The access-control intent and the implemented check do not match; use an explicit admin/owner scope check if the feature is meant to be privileged, and fix the misleading comment.

Comment claims a behavior change that the code does not make

The added comment in `Cursor.__init__` ("Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios") describes a change, but the only code here is the pre-existing `self.offset = int(offset)`; nothing about negative offsets was enabled or validated. The comment misleads future readers into believing negative offsets are an intentionally supported/validated feature of `Cursor`, when in fact consumers such as `OffsetPaginator` still raise `BadPaginationError` for them. Remove or correct it.

No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new query parameter

The PR adds a new public paginator class with its own `get_result` implementation and a new request-controlled branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` (`?optimized_pagination=true`), but no tests are added for either. The paginator's datetime key handling and negative-offset path are both broken (see other findings), which a single test exercising the endpoint with the new parameter would have caught. Add tests covering: the optimized branch for an eligible user, a non-member/superuser requester (where `organization_context.member` is None), and a negative-offset cursor.

Silent clamping of negative offsets changes pagination semantics and is inconsistent for prev cursors

`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in `BasePaginator.get_result` silently rewrites a client-supplied negative forward offset to 0, so the response no longer corresponds to the requested cursor; the next/prev cursors produced by `build_cursor` are still derived from the original (negative) `cursor.offset`, so clients can get duplicated or skipped rows instead of a clear error. Meanwhile the `is_prev` branch still passes a negative offset straight into the queryset slice, which Django rejects with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (500). Invalid offsets should be rejected uniformly with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-clamped.

get_result duplicated from BasePaginator, dropping explanatory invariants

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` (~60 lines) with the inline documentation about the extra before-row fetch removed. Any future fix to the base implementation (e.g. the cursor-value comparison edge case documented in the base method) will silently not apply here. Prefer overriding only the slice computation via a small hook instead of copying the whole method.

value_from_cursor returns a raw number for a datetime column, producing an invalid WHERE clause

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged (integer/float), but `BasePaginator.build_queryset` injects it into `WHERE "auditlogentry"."datetime" >= %s`. For the audit-log endpoint the sort key is a timestamp column, so comparing it against a bare millisecond integer either raises a database error or silently filters wrong rows. `DateTimePaginator` converts the cursor value back to a `datetime` for exactly this reason; this subclass must do the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative slice start raises ValueError in Django, not a handled pagination error

In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). The inline comment claims "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", which is false: Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative indices with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` Every other paginator in this file guards this with `raise BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. The result is an unhandled exception and a 500 response that is trivially triggered by any client passing a cursor such as `-5:0:0`, i.e. a cheap error/DoS vector on the audit log endpoint.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets, producing inconsistent cursors

`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes `BasePaginator.get_result` so that a negative forward offset is silently clamped to 0 instead of surfacing an error. Two problems: (1) an invalid/garbage cursor now returns page-1 data as if it were valid, masking client bugs; (2) the raw negative `offset` is still passed on to `build_cursor` and still used in the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down, so the drop-extra-row logic and the generated next/prev cursor offsets no longer correspond to the rows actually fetched. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still handed to Django and will raise. If clamping is desired it should be applied consistently (and the invalid case rejected with `BadPaginationError`).

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime columns, but is used with order_by="-datetime"

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `math.floor(value)/math.ceil(value)` on the raw attribute and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value, i.e. it only works for numeric keys (it is a copy of `Paginator`, not `DateTimePaginator`). The audit-log endpoint instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"` on `AuditLogEntry.datetime` (a DateTimeField). `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])`, so `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`, and on a follow-up request `build_queryset` injects an integer into `WHERE "datetime" <= %s`, comparing an int against a timestamp column. Any request to the new code path fails with a 500 or a database error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
organization_context.member may be None, causing a 500 on the audit log endpoint

`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` unconditionally whenever `is_superuser` is false. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `None` for callers that are not org members — notably org auth tokens / integration tokens and staff or superuser-flagged users accessing an org they do not belong to — so the expression raises `AttributeError` and turns a previously working GET into a 500. This runs for every request, not just when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed.

false_positives.candidate:
"Advanced pagination" gate is not an admin check

The comment says the feature is enabled for "authorized administrators", but the gate is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `request.user.is_superuser` is the raw DB flag and bypasses Sentry's required active-superuser/elevated-session check (`is_active_superuser(request)`), and `has_global_access` is true for ordinary members in open-membership organizations. So the out-of-bounds pagination path (negative offsets, no `BadPaginationError` guard) is reachable by regular org members and by superuser-flagged sessions that have not elevated. Feature flags that relax pagination bounds should be gated on an explicit permission check, not on these two signals.

Eviction limit hard-coded at 1000 while max_segment_spans config is now dead

The new eviction (`if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`) hard-codes the segment span limit in Lua, while `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` which, after the removal of the count check in `_load_segment_data`, is no longer referenced anywhere. Operators changing `max_segment_spans` now silently get no effect, and the two values disagree (1000 vs 1001). The limit should be passed to the script as an ARGV, or the unused parameter removed.

Module docstring/glossary still describes plain Redis sets

The module docstring ("Add the ingested span's payload to the set under `set_key`", and the glossary entry "span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys") is now wrong: these keys are sorted sets scored by `end_timestamp_precise`, and the scoring is what drives the new eviction behaviour. Readers relying on the docstring will not know spans are evicted lowest-timestamp-first once a segment exceeds 1000 spans.

No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint query parameter

`OptimizedCursorPaginator` (including the negative-offset branch) and the new `optimized_pagination=true` branch in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` are added with no test coverage in this PR. Both are trivially broken (negative slice raises in Django, `get_item_key` cannot handle datetimes) which a single endpoint test with `?optimized_pagination=true` would have caught.

Redirect-chain limit silently lowered from 10000 to 1000

The loop bound was changed from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000` and the explanatory comment ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. This is an unannounced behaviour change: segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will no longer be joined into a single segment, producing split segments for deep traces. If the reduction is intentional it should be documented and the retained comment updated; the PR description mentions nothing about it.

Set keys switched to sorted sets without renaming, breaking rolling deploys with WRONGTYPE

`span-buf:s:{...}` keys change type from Redis SET to ZSET (`p.zadd` here, `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua, `p.zscan` in `_load_segment_data`) while keeping the exact same key names. During a rolling deploy (and for up to `redis_ttl` = 1h after it) old SET keys written by the previous version still exist; `zadd`/`zcard` against them return `WRONGTYPE`, which aborts the Lua script and raises out of `p.execute()`, crash-looping the consumer. Old pods still running will likewise get `WRONGTYPE` from `sadd`/`sscan` on the new ZSET keys. The key prefix needs a version bump (e.g. `span-buf:z:`) so the two formats cannot collide.

Span eviction is now silent: no metric or log when spans are dropped

The removed block in `_load_segment_data` emitted `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged when a segment exceeded the span count limit. The replacement — `zpopmin` inside add-buffer.lua — drops spans with no counter and no log, so oversized-segment truncation becomes invisible in production and silent data loss cannot be detected or quantified. The script should return the number of evicted members so the consumer can emit a metric.

Unguarded access to end_timestamp_precise can crash the consumer

`end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` uses direct indexing (unlike the neighbouring `val.get(...)` calls), so any message on the ingest-spans topic missing this field raises `KeyError` inside `process_batch` and kills the consumer rather than dropping/DLQ-ing the bad message. Given this is a newly required field, in-flight messages produced by older Relay versions would take the consumer down.

zunionstore uses default SUM aggregation, corrupting timestamp scores

`zunionstore set_key 2 set_key span_key` (and the same call for `parent_key`) uses Redis' default `AGGREGATE SUM`. Any span payload present in both source zsets — which happens on duplicate deliveries / reprocessing of the same span — gets its score set to the sum of the two `end_timestamp_precise` values, roughly doubling it. Since the score is used as the eviction ordering key for `zpopmin`, such a span becomes effectively un-evictable while legitimate newer spans are dropped instead. Pass `AGGREGATE MIN` (or MAX) explicitly to keep scores meaningful.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility computed from outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first argument but passes the closure-level `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`) `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (`discover`, `split_dataset`, etc.) while the outer `dataset` is still the metrics/transactions dataset. As a result the dataset-based gate (`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) is evaluated against the wrong dataset: upsampling can be skipped for error queries actually run against `discover`, or applied to a run that was switched to a transaction-like dataset. The check must use `scoped_dataset`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed

The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is an accidentally committed nested checkout of the repository itself; `git submodule update --init` will fail for anyone cloning, and tooling that walks the tree (mypy `files = ["."]`, pytest collection) can behave unpredictably. It should be removed from the commit.

Blanket `except Exception: pass` hides malformed error_sampling fixtures

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the `float()` conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. If a test supplies a malformed `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or `contexts` not being a mapping), `sample_rate` is silently not set and the test will then assert on non-upsampled counts, masking the real problem instead of failing loudly. Since this only runs in test fixtures, the errors should propagate (or at least be narrowed to `TypeError/ValueError` with an assertion).

Caching a global option behind a per-org/per-project key yields stale, inconsistent results

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the result of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` for 60s under a key built from `organization.id` plus a hash of the project id set. The underlying data is the *global* option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, which Sentry's options layer already caches in-process; writing/reading a remote cache entry per org+project-set combination adds a cache round trip per query (and the split-dataset path calls this up to 4 times per request) while providing no real speedup. Worse, when the allowlist is changed, queries keep returning the previous decision for up to 60 seconds, so the same chart can flip between upsampled (x10) and raw counts between adjacent requests - a visible data-correctness problem for a counting API. Either drop the cache or key it on the option value/version.

No test covers the new caching entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`

The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and the column transform. The public function added by this PR - including the cache key construction, cache hit/miss behaviour, and the interaction between a cached `False`/`True` and the dataset gate - is completely untested, which is exactly where the risky logic (stale cache, hash-based key) lives. Tests should at minimum cover a cache hit returning the stale decision and the empty-project-ids case.

Substring match treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused

`_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring test `"event.type:error" in query`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) or `event.type:error_foo` also contains that substring, so the function returns True. For the `discover` dataset this causes `count()` to be rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (i.e. `sum(sample_weight)`) for a query that explicitly excludes error events, producing wrong numbers for transaction/other rows (or a Snuba error because `sample_weight` is not populated for non-error rows). The check needs to parse the search query (or at least exclude negations) rather than a naive substring test.

Test comments contradict the asserted values

`assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10  # First bucket has 1 event` (and the following line) claim the bucket contains 1 event while asserting 10. The 10 comes from the 0.1 client sample rate being upsampled; the comments should state that, otherwise a future reader will assume the assertion is wrong and "fix" it.

`hash()` of project ids in the cache key can collide and return another project set's decision
