The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. `hash` is a 64-bit (32-bit on some builds) value with no collision guarantees, so two different project-id sets inside the same organization can map to the same key. When that happens a non-allowlisted project set will reuse the cached `True` of an allowlisted set (or vice versa), silently multiplying counts by the sample weight for projects that are not configured for upsampling. Use the actual sorted ids (or a cryptographic digest) in the key instead of `hash()`.

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is dead code and cannot actually invalidate the cache

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the PR, although its docstring states it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency". It also cannot fulfil that promise: the cache key depends on an arbitrary project-id subset, so invalidating after an allowlist change would require enumerating every org/project-id combination that was ever queried. This leaves the misleading impression that stale cache entries are handled, when in practice they are not.

`upsampled_count` declares result type `number` although it returns an integer

The aggregate is wrapped in `toInt64`, and the function replaces `count()` (declared `default_result_type="integer"` elsewhere in this file), but it declares `default_result_type="number"`. The response `meta` will advertise a different field type than `count()` does, which changes client-side formatting/axis handling for the very charts this feature rewrites.

`upsampled_count` is exposed as a public discover function with no project gating

The new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is registered without `private=True` (unlike the neighbouring internal functions), so any API consumer can now request `upsampled_count()` as a field/yAxis on arbitrary discover queries. The aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which is only meaningful for error rows in allowlisted projects; for transactions or non-upsampled errors it will either error out on the missing/unset `sample_weight` column or return meaningless values, bypassing the allowlist checks in `error_upsampling.py` entirely. Mark it private so only the internal transformation can use it.

`upsampled_count` only registered for the discover dataset while the errors dataset path returns True

`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` unconditionally returns True for `dataset == errors`, so `count()` will be rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count` for errors-dataset queries. However the function is only added to `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter` in this file; the errors dataset uses its own dataset config/function converter. Unless `upsampled_count` is resolvable there, every errors-dataset timeseries query from an allowlisted project will fail with an "unknown function" validation error. No test in this PR exercises `dataset=errors`, so this path is unverified.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error IDs are paired with nodestore data by dict ordering

`fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node id; its iteration order is not guaranteed to match the order of the input list (and backends may omit/reorder keys, e.g. when some come from cache). As a result an `ErrorEvent` can be built with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of a different one, and if any node is missing the remaining pairings shift by one. The ids/messages that end up in the Seer prompt and in the summary can therefore be wrong. Iterate over `node_ids` and look up `events[node_id]` instead of relying on dict order.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged table path renders an empty table, discarding widget data

When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — the actual `result`/`fields`/`meta` for the widget are ignored. Any organization with the flag enabled will see every dashboard table widget render with no headers and no rows. Either pass the real `result` data/columns or don't wire the flag up until the mapping exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so 0 values bypass validation

`validate_timestamp` rejects a report when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy and `validate_age` when `timestamp` is truthy. `age: 0` (a report generated just now, which is the common case for freshly queued reports) and `timestamp: 0` are falsy, so a report containing both fields is accepted when one of them is 0, and conversely the validation message is never triggered for the most frequent values. Compare against `None` (`is not None`) instead of truthiness.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics event recorded before the feature flag / validation checks

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any schema validation, so every request from orgs without the feature (and every malformed request) is counted as an assemble call. This inflates the metric and makes it useless for measuring real usage; move the record after the feature gate, or add a flag/result attribute.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

false_positives.candidate:
60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity auth refresh chunk

`check_auth_identities` iterates over up to `chunk_size=100` identities, each performing a network `provider.refresh_identity(...)`, and then re-schedules `check_auth` to continue the chain. With a 60s processing deadline the task can be killed mid-batch; because `check_auth` already bumped `last_synced` for the whole chunk before enqueuing, those identities are skipped for ~a day and, more importantly, the follow-up `check_auth.apply_async` at the end of the function never runs, so the batching chain stops. Size the deadline to the worst case (chunk_size × per-identity refresh latency) or make the reschedule happen before the refresh loop.

Error/replay timestamps compared in different units, so errors are never interleaved

`gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, which is Unix time in **seconds**, while rrweb replay event timestamps are Unix time in **milliseconds**. Every error timestamp is therefore smaller than every replay event timestamp, so all error log lines are flushed before the first breadcrumb instead of being interleaved chronologically — defeating the purpose of this change. The unit tests hide this because the fixture segment uses second-scale timestamps (1.5, 2.0). Normalize both to the same unit (e.g. multiply error timestamps by 1000) before comparing.

Header alignment computed from display name instead of column key

`fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type)` uses the human-readable column name. When callers override `name` (the documented use case, e.g. `name: 'Count of Span Duration'` for key `count(span.duration)`), `fieldAlignment` can no longer recognize the aggregate/field and will align numeric columns as if they were strings. Pass `column.key` to `fieldAlignment` and keep `column.name` only for the rendered label.

Inconsistent optional chaining will throw when meta is absent

`Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` guards `tableData` but not `meta`, so if `tableData` is supplied without `meta` (the type requires it, but callers pass loosely-typed API data) this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Elsewhere in the same component `tableData?.data ?? []` is defensive, so the intent was clearly to tolerate missing data. Use `tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}`.

Issue template embeds a trailing newline while callers also join with newlines

`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` ends with `\n`, but both `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` join the rendered lines with `"\n"`. The posted comment therefore contains a blank line between every issue and an extra blank line before the footer (visible in the updated test expectations). If the double spacing is not intended, drop the trailing newline from the template.

No-op migrations point at a replacement migration that is not in this change

Both 0917 and 0920 are gutted with the comment "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no such file is added in this PR. If 0921 does not exist, the org saved-search → view backfill is now silently never performed and the comment misleads the next reader. Add the replacement migration (or fix the reference).

One invalid report in a batch discards the entire batch

The loop returns HTTP 422 as soon as any single report in the posted array fails validation, so none of the valid reports in that batch are counted by the `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` metric. Browsers batch multiple reports per request and will keep re-sending the same batch, so a single malformed/unsupported report (e.g. a non-RFC URL, or a type outside `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES`) permanently blinds the collector for that client. Prefer skipping+logging invalid entries and still processing the valid ones.

attributes can now be undefined and query defaults changed

The rewritten hook returns `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data`, where `data` is `TagCollection | undefined`; previously the hook always returned an object (`{}` at minimum), so consumers that spread/iterate the result (e.g. building filter key sections) can now receive `undefined` on error or before the first fetch. Additionally, the move from `useApiQuery` (which set `retry: false`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`) to a bare `useQuery` reinstates the default retry/refetch-on-focus behaviour, and the `environment` parameter that was previously sent is now dropped. Default `data` to `{}` and re-apply the query options if the previous behaviour was intended.

error_ids silently dropped when caller passes `field` query params

`process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` filters the replay payload down to the requested fields, and then `error_ids` is read from the filtered response. Any caller that supplies `?field=...` without `error_ids` (a legal request for this endpoint signature) will get `error_ids = []` and lose all error context with no indication why. Read `error_ids` from the unfiltered snuba response, or hardcode the field list used for this internal lookup.

get_environment_info issues a Snuba/nodestore fetch per issue in PR comments

`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment (up to 5 per comment, for both GitHub and GitLab workflows). `get_recommended_event` runs a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, so each PR comment now performs several extra round trips in the comment task that previously only used the already-loaded `Group` rows. Consider fetching the latest/recommended events in bulk, or deriving the environment from data already available on the group.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write and can be raced

The code list is read in the earlier `prisma.user.findUnique`, mutated in memory (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and written back with a full `update`. Two concurrent login attempts that both read the same ciphertext can both succeed with the *same* backup code, and the second write will also resurrect codes consumed by the first attempt (last write wins). Backup codes are meant to be single use; this allows replay of a code that was already spent. Consumption needs to be atomic (e.g. a transaction with a conditional update / optimistic version check on the stored value).

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
resetState leaves stale backup codes and leaks the blob object URL

`resetState()` clears only `password`, `errorMessage` and `step`. `backupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl` are kept, so after closing and reopening the dialog the previously generated codes and download URL remain in component state (and are still reachable by the download anchor until a new setup overwrites them). The object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked on the next successful setup, so dialogs that are cancelled leak the blob for the lifetime of the document. Clear `backupCodes` and revoke/clear `backupCodesUrl` in `resetState` (and on unmount).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

false_positives.candidate:
"missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such option exists

The message "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown (login page and disable modal) when `user.backupCodes` is null. Every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has null `backupCodes` (the migration does not backfill), and this PR adds no UI to generate codes for an already-enabled 2FA account — codes are only created by `totp/setup`, which rejects users with `twoFactorEnabled` true. Users following this instruction will find nothing in settings; the only route is disabling 2FA (which requires a working authenticator) and re-enabling. Either add a regeneration flow or change the message to reflect reality.

Assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op and was documented rather than fixed

`expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise, which is always truthy, so the first test never verifies that 2FA was actually enabled (the added FIXME admits this). Use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or the `[data-state="checked"]` selector used in the second test so the test can actually fail.

Backup code can be used to log in without the account password

The credentials provider only verifies the password when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` a few lines above). The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is true, regardless of `totpCode`. An attacker can therefore POST `email` + empty `password` + any garbage `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") + a valid `backupCode` and be logged in without ever proving knowledge of the password. Unlike a TOTP code, a backup code is static and never expires, so a single leaked/stolen backup code becomes a standalone, long-lived credential for the account. The backup-code check should require a successful password verification (or at minimum must not be reachable on the password-skipping path).

Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed

Backup codes are persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, i.e. recoverable plaintext for anyone with the DB dump and the shared app encryption key (the same key used for many other things and typically present in the app environment). Because a backup code bypasses 2FA entirely, these should be stored as one-way hashes and compared by hashing the submitted value, so a database/key compromise does not immediately yield usable 2FA-bypass credentials. Additionally each code carries only 40 bits of entropy (`crypto.randomBytes(5)`), which is low for a credential that is checked by an endpoint reachable by unauthenticated callers.

No test covers the actual backup-code authentication paths

The only added coverage exercises the download/copy/close buttons on the new setup screen. The security-critical new logic — logging in with a backup code via the credentials provider (including single-use consumption) and disabling 2FA with a backup code in `totp/disable.ts` — has no test at all, as the added TODO acknowledges. Given this code path can authenticate a user, at least one test that logs in with a stored code and asserts the code cannot be reused should be added.

Unvalidated/unguarded backup code handling can throw an unhandled 500

`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, key))` and `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` are not guarded: if the stored ciphertext was written with a different `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (decrypt/parse throws) or if a client sends a non-string `backupCode` (e.g. a number or object), the handler throws a raw exception and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a meaningful error code. Validate the request body type and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning a defined ErrorCode.

onEnable() is now deferred to the Close button, so dismissing the dialog desyncs UI and loses the codes

Previously `onEnable()` was invoked as soon as the enable request succeeded; now it is only called from the "Close" button on the `DisplayBackupCodes` step. If the user dismisses the dialog with ESC/outside click/X after 2FA was already enabled server side, the parent is never notified: the two-factor switch stays in the "off" state even though 2FA is enabled on the account, and the backup codes are gone forever (there is no regenerate path). Notify the parent as soon as the server confirms enablement, and/or handle `onOpenChange` on this step.

tabIndex={-1} makes the password reveal toggle unreachable by keyboard

Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button removes it from the tab order globally for every `PasswordField` in the app, so keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer toggle password visibility (the `sr-only` label and tooltip become unreachable). If the intent was only to keep focus out of the way in the 2FA modals, this should not be applied to the shared component unconditionally.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Destination-calendar fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match

`event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares each `externalId` against `undefined`/`null` and always returns `undefined`. The pre-change fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Consequence: when a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, `calendar.events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` (request fails / wrong target) instead of the configured destination calendar. The same broken predicate is used at line 317 in `deleteEvent`, where it silently falls back to `primary` and the event in the destination calendar is never deleted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug logic inverted (unrelated change)

The condition was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the behaviour: the team's `slug` is now only persisted when team billing *is* enabled, and in that case both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` are set simultaneously. On self-hosted/billing-disabled instances the organization is now created with `slug = null`, so its subdomain/org lookup (`orgDomains`, `slugCollisions` checks, org URLs) will not resolve. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and should be reverted or corrected to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent may be called with an undefined credential

Inside the `reference.credentialId` branch, if neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB lookup yields a credential (e.g. credential deleted, or app slug missing), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still invoked, which will throw when it dereferences `credential.appName`/`credential.type`. Guard with `if (credential)` and push a failed `EventResult` otherwise so the booking flow reports the app status instead of hitting the generic catch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Invalid dynamicUserList surfaces as 500 instead of 400

`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is caught by the new try/catch, which only maps `HttpError` and `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to a 400; a plain `Error` falls through to `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. A malformed client request therefore reports a server error and the real reason is lost. Throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for this validation.

No tests for multi-destination-calendar creation/update paths

`createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents` were substantially rewritten (loops over multiple destination calendars, per-reference credential resolution, DB credential fallback), and `EventResult.externalId`/`credentialId` now drive `referencesToCreate`. There are no unit tests covering: multiple destination calendars producing one reference per calendar with the correct `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId`, the empty destinationCalendar fallback, and the video-reference credentialId. Given the regressions these fields cause in cancel/reschedule flows, tests here would prevent silent breakage.

Recurring cancellation deletes every event once per calendar reference

The recurring-event branch (iterating all of the user's calendar credentials × all `updatedBookings` × each booking's first calendar reference) is now executed inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references the same delete requests are issued N times, multiplying external API calls and producing repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring branch should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop (or keyed on the current reference) instead of re-running for each one.

Team destination calendars dropped when organizer has none

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and the collective branch then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because of the optional chaining the collected host calendars are silently discarded in exactly the case the PR aims to fix (organizer without a destination calendar, other collective hosts with one). Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) and push, or build the array from all sources before assigning.

TypeError when location is Google Meet and no destination calendar exists

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null, and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose organizer/event type has no destination calendar (previously handled safely via `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), `EventManager.create()` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, failing the whole booking instead of falling back to Cal Video.

Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar is now inconsistent (null vs [] vs array)

`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` changed from an object to an array, which is a breaking change for webhook/API consumers. The payload is now inconsistent across triggers: BOOKING_REJECTED expects `[]` (confirm.handler returns `[]`), while BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect `null` (handleNewBooking assigns `null` when no calendar is found). Normalize to a single representation (always an array) and document the breaking payload change.

createEvent falls back to "primary" when destination calendar has no credentialId

`selectedCalendar` is now resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. Destination calendars stored without a `credentialId` (legacy rows, and the event-type destination calendar path in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` which calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an externalId) will not match, so the event is created in the account's `primary` calendar instead of the user-selected destination calendar. Previously `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId` was used unconditionally. Consider keeping an `externalId` fallback when no credentialId match is found.

credentialId is no longer stored for video booking references

`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the previous code stored `result.credentialId` for video results. Cancellation logic in `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`), so video meetings created after this change will never be deleted on cancellation, and other code paths that resolve a video credential from the reference will also break.

events.patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId

The insert call guards with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to write the hangout link into the description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When `selectedCalendar` is undefined (no destination calendar matching the credentialId), the event is created in `primary` but the patch request targets an undefined calendar and fails, so Google Meet links are missing from the calendar event description.

organization.slug removed from dynamic-booking user select

The rewritten `loadUsers` for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which the previous query included. Any downstream consumer of the organizer's `organization.slug` (org-aware booker/webapp URLs) will now see `undefined` for dynamic group bookings. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor; restore the field unless it is provably unused.

updateAllCalendarEvents error is no longer logged

The `catch` block still builds the diagnostic `message` string (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed, so `message` is now dead code and calendar-update failures are swallowed with no trace in the logs. Either log the message or remove it.

updateLocation no longer records externalCalendarId on references

`referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation` now uses `result.externalId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId` on its `EventResult` (only `createEvent` does). Previously the value came from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result, booking references recreated after a location change get `externalCalendarId: undefined`, so later updates/cancellations can no longer target the correct external calendar (see the Google `deleteEvent`/`updateEvent` fallbacks, which require it).

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token", destroying valid stored refresh tokens

When the provider response has no `refresh_token`, the function sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. This runs on the normal (non credential-sharing) path too. For providers whose schema makes `refresh_token` optional — e.g. `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, where the result is spread with `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and persisted — the real, still-valid refresh token in the DB is overwritten with the useless string `"refresh_token"`, so the next refresh fails and the user must reconnect. Only inject a placeholder when it is actually needed, or leave the field absent so the spread keeps the existing token.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are nonsense and strip every token field except access_token

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string `"[object Object]"` (Zod types have no `toString` override), so the object literal ends up with a single extra key literally named `"[object Object]"`, with the second definition overwriting the first. The resulting schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown }`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when credential sharing is enabled the parsed data loses `expires_in`/`expiry_date`/`refresh_token`/`scope`/etc. Callers that spread `tokenResponse.data` into the stored credential (e.g. office365calendar) will therefore persist a credential with no expiry and a bogus refresh token. The intent ("allow any extra properties, require access_token plus a numeric expiry") needs `.passthrough()` / `z.record()`, not computed keys.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)` (i.e. `{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed object, but the return value is assigned to `key` and written straight into `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously the code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the credential object itself. As a result, after the first token refresh the stored Google Calendar credential becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, which no longer satisfies `googleCredentialSchema` on the next load, permanently breaking Google Calendar for that user. It should store `...data` (and ideally only after checking `success`).

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync path returns a fetch Response where callers expect an axios/SDK/gaxios response

When credential sharing is enabled the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, but the call sites consume very different shapes: `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios response), `hubspot` assigns the return value to a `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken` (SDK object), and `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data` (gaxios response). A `Response` has none of these properties, so with `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` configured these refresh paths throw `TypeError` or silently store `undefined` tokens. The helper needs to normalise the sync response per call site (or each call site must handle both shapes).

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync path returns a fetch Response where callers expect an axios/SDK/gaxios response

When credential sharing is enabled the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, but the call sites consume very different shapes: `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios response), `hubspot` assigns the return value to a `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken` (SDK object), and `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data` (gaxios response). A `Response` has none of these properties, so with `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` configured these refresh paths throw `TypeError` or silently store `undefined` tokens. The helper needs to normalise the sync response per call site (or each call site must handle both shapes).

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zoho-bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId

`refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` — the third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com `userId`, which is sent to the external sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Passing the credential's id means that, with credential sharing enabled, the self-hosted endpoint is queried for the wrong user, so either the request fails or (worse) another user's tokens are fetched and stored on this credential. `refreshAccessToken` should receive and forward `credential.userId`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Refresh success is checked via `response.statusText !== "OK"`

`statusText` is not guaranteed to be populated (HTTP/2 and several fetch implementations return an empty string for a 200 response), so this check can throw `HttpError` with an empty message on a perfectly successful token refresh, and it also treats any non-200 2xx as success. Use `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce connection is built with the stale access token after refreshing

`getClient` fetches a new access token and stores it in the DB, but then constructs `new jsforce.Connection({ ..., accessToken: credentialKey.access_token })` using the *old* token from the credential instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` (and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` instead of the refreshed `instance_url`). The refresh is therefore pointless: all subsequent API calls still use the expired token and will fail with 401/INVALID_SESSION_ID.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unvalidated request body and decryption failures produce unhandled 500s; no HTTP method guard

`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed payload, and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` / `JSON.parse(...)` throw on a bad key or non-JSON plaintext. None of these are caught, so the handler returns an unhandled 500 (with a stack trace in the logs/response depending on config) instead of a 400 with a useful message. There is also no method check, so a `GET`/`DELETE` to this route reaches the body parse and 500s. Use `safeParse` + explicit 400s and restrict the handler to POST.

false_positives.candidate:
Credential sync request carries no authentication and its status is never checked

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret/signature (contrast with the inbound webhook, which requires `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The remote endpoint therefore cannot distinguish a request from Cal.com from any other caller, so an endpoint implemented as documented hands out user access tokens to anyone who can reach it. The response status is also never checked, so an error page/HTML body is passed on to the caller as if it were a token response. A signed header (or reuse of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and an `response.ok` check are needed, and the expected request/response contract should be documented.

No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token parsing helper

This PR adds a new unauthenticated-by-default HTTP surface that writes OAuth credentials into the database (`/api/webhook/app-credential`) plus two shared helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that are now on the refresh path of ~10 apps, and ships with no unit/integration tests (the PR description confirms this). Given that the helpers change the stored credential shape for Google, Office365, Salesforce and others, regressions here silently break every user's calendar/video integrations. At minimum, tests covering secret rejection, create vs update behaviour, and the enabled/disabled branches of the two helpers should be added.

Salesforce refreshes the token and writes the credential on every service instantiation

The new refresh_token request and `prisma.credential.update` run unconditionally inside `getClient`, which is called from the constructor. There is no expiry check (unlike every other app, which only refreshes when the stored token is expired). Every Salesforce CalendarService creation — including availability lookups — now issues a token request to `login.salesforce.com` plus a DB write, which wastes requests, risks hitting Salesforce's OAuth rate limits, and adds latency to the booking path. Gate the refresh on the stored expiry.

Synced credential update does not clear the `invalid` flag

When a credential already exists the handler only updates `key`. Credentials that were previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. by `invalidateCredential` in the Zoom/Webex adapters, or the `invalid_grant` path in Google Calendar) stay flagged after fresh working keys are pushed in, so Cal.com keeps treating the app as broken and shows the "reconnect" state even though the parent application has supplied valid tokens. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

Webhook secret compared with `!==` (non constant-time) and header lookup is case-sensitive

The shared secret check uses a plain string comparison, which is vulnerable to timing analysis; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Additionally, `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` relies on the operator configuring a lowercase header name (Node lowercases incoming header keys); if they configure `Calcom-Webhook-Secret` every request silently 403s. Lowercase the configured name before the lookup instead of only documenting the requirement in `.env.example`.

Zoom sends appSlug "zoomvideo" while the app's slug is "zoom"

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the credential sync endpoint, but the Zoom app's slug everywhere else in the codebase (and in the `App` table / the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` lookup) is `zoom` — see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` which creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`. The self-hoster therefore receives an identifier that does not match the slug it must post back, so Zoom credential syncing cannot work without a special case.

`prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService

`await prisma.credential.update(...)` was added to `getClient`, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in the file (the import list only adds `zod` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). This is a compile error under type-check and a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, which means every Salesforce CalendarService instantiation (i.e. every booking/availability call involving Salesforce) will throw.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased list

`blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased when parsed from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the incoming guest email is compared raw (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Any blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. `Spam@example.com`) bypasses the blacklist and is added as an attendee, defeating the purpose of the environment variable. Lowercase the guest before comparison.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team permission check uses AND instead of OR

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user can be either an admin or the owner, not normally both as reported by these two helpers, so this expression is effectively always false and team admins/owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will always get a FORBIDDEN error. It should be `||`. (Also note `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` queries membership for team id 0 for personal bookings, which is a misleading fallback.)

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Emails are keyed off the unfiltered input list, not the actually-added guests

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input array instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in this list decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("you were invited") or the "guests added" notification. If a submitted email was filtered out because it is already an attendee, that existing attendee incorrectly receives a brand-new booking confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest list is not de-duplicated or case-normalized before insert

`uniqueGuests` only filters guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and non-lowercased blacklist entries; it does not de-duplicate the incoming array itself. The tRPC input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also allows duplicates. A direct API call with `guests: ["a@a.com", "a@a.com"]` (or `A@a.com` for an existing attendee) will create duplicate attendee rows for the same booking, producing duplicate emails and corrupt attendee lists. Dedupe case-insensitively server-side and compare existing attendee emails case-insensitively.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable metadata

Every other sender in this file (e.g. `sendLocationChangeEmails`) guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and accepts an `eventTypeMetadata` argument. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always sends to both host and attendees, so event types configured with `disableStandardEmails` will still send organizer and attendee emails, violating that setting.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
CalendarEvent is built without team info, so team hosts are never notified

`sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts, but the `evt` constructed here never sets `team` (the booking query doesn't load the event type's hosts/users either). For team or round-robin bookings, no team member other than the booking owner receives the guests-added email, unlike the location-change flow which populates team members.

Copy-pasted comment claims a 40kb payload

The comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" was copied from the PhoneInput/AddressInput lazy wrappers. `MultiEmail` is a small component with no heavy third-party dependency, so the comment misstates the reason for the dynamic import and will mislead future maintainers.

Email failure is swallowed without logging the error

`catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely, so any failure to notify guests/organizers is undiagnosable in production. Use the project `logger` and include the error and bookingId.

Error toast shows raw tRPC error code and the fallback message is dead code

`const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` can never fall back to the friendly message. Users will see strings like `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` (and `undefined: ...` when `err.data` is missing). Build the message from the translated key only, falling back to `unable_to_add_guests`.

ICS attachment lacks iCalUID/sequence, likely creating duplicate calendar entries

The `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` sets only `uid` and omits `iCalUID` / `iCalSequence` (both stored on the booking). The generated ICS is sent with `method: "REQUEST"`, so recipients' calendar clients will treat it as a new invite with a different UID rather than an update to the existing event, resulting in duplicate calendar entries for the attendees who already had the booking.

Invalid-email error never clears and empty list silently does nothing

`handleAdd` sets `isInvalidEmail` to true on failure but never resets it to false on a subsequent successful validation or on dialog reopen, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" warning stays visible after the user fixes the input. Additionally, when the user removes all email rows (`multiEmailValue.length === 0`), clicking Add returns silently with no user feedback.

MultiEmail imports its own package barrel, creating a circular dependency

`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports `MultiEmailLazy` -> `MultiEmail`. This import cycle can yield `undefined` components at runtime depending on module evaluation order, and it pulls the entire UI barrel into the dynamically imported chunk, defeating the purpose of the lazy wrapper. Import the components from their concrete module paths (e.g. `../components/button`, `../components/form`) as the other `form/*` components do.

New mutation has no tests

`addGuestsHandler` contains non-trivial authorization logic, guest filtering/blacklisting and email fan-out, but no unit or e2e test is added in this PR. At minimum the permission matrix (organizer / attendee / team admin / unrelated user) and the duplicate/blacklisted-guest filtering should be covered, since the authorization expression is currently inverted and would have been caught by a test.

No guard against adding guests to seated, cancelled or past bookings

The handler adds attendees to any booking regardless of `status` or `seatsPerTimeSlot`. For seated event types, remaining seats are derived from the attendee count and each real seat has a `BookingSeat` reference; inserting plain attendees here silently consumes seats without seat references, corrupting seat availability. For past or cancelled bookings (the "Edit" actions menu is also rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem), new guests receive a confirmation email and ICS for an event that already happened. Validate booking status and reject seated event types.

Subject line dereferences attendees[0] without a guard

`name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if `attendees` is empty, and renders an empty name when the first attendee has no name (newly added guests are created with `name: ""`). Other organizer templates guard this (e.g. fall back to the organizer/team name). Since the email send is wrapped in a bare `catch` in the handler, such a failure would be silently swallowed and no organizer email sent.

findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` throws an opaque 500 for bookings without a user

`prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` will throw a Prisma `NotFoundError` (surfacing as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client) for any booking whose `userId` is null, e.g. dynamic group bookings. Handle the null case explicitly with a proper TRPCError, or derive the organizer from the already-included `booking.user` relation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic retryCount update can lose increments

`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` computes the new value from the value read earlier in the request. If two cron invocations overlap (or the job is retried while a previous run is still processing), both read the same value and write the same result, losing an increment and allowing more retries than intended. Use Prisma's atomic update `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead. Same issue at line 195.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteMany retryCount clause is not scoped to SMS reminders

The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` call has no `method` filter, so this SMS-only cron will delete *any* WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, mandatory reminders, etc.) whose retryCount exceeds 1, including rows that were already successfully scheduled. Any future code path that increments retryCount for a non-SMS method will silently have its reminders purged by this endpoint. The branch should be combined with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

false_positives.candidate:
Prisma update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the top of the `catch` block is itself unawaited-by-try: if it rejects (e.g. the reminder row was deleted concurrently → Prisma P2025 record-not-found), the rejection escapes the catch, aborts the remaining reminders in the loop and returns a 500 instead of the intended per-reminder error handling. Wrap it in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`, which does not throw on no match).

retryCount filter in deleteMany has no supporting index

The new `retryCount` column is used in a `deleteMany` predicate (`retryCount > 1`) that runs on every cron invocation, but no index covers it and the existing indexes (`[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]`, `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`) do not help because the predicate is an unscoped OR branch. On a large WorkflowReminder table this forces a sequential scan each run. Scoping the branch to method/scheduled (so an existing index can be used) or adding an index would avoid the repeated full-table scan.

retryCount is never incremented when sendTo/message is missing, so reminders are retried forever

The retryCount increment only happens inside the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` block (else branch) or in the `catch`. When `sendTo` is null/empty (e.g. a booking with no `smsReminderNumber`, which is one of the main failure modes this PR targets) or the rendered message is empty, the loop silently does nothing: the reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and will be re-processed on every cron run until the scheduled date passes. The same applies to the `continue` at line 69 when `workflowStep`/`booking` is missing. These cases should also bump retryCount (or delete the reminder).

true_positives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` instance (never null/undefined — it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` on failure), so `authConditions` is always truthy and the `else if (filterConditions)` / final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branches at lines 76-80 can never execute. This dead code hides the fact that the "no authorization" case is already represented by `1=0`; it should be simplified to avoid future readers assuming a null-auth path exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Caching tests deleted without replacement

The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching behaviour still exists in the service (lines 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts) and is now untested, so a regression (e.g. the `=== undefined` check for the nullable filter cache) would go unnoticed. The tests could have been ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations like the others.

Constructor options type widened, losing discriminated-union safety

The constructor parameter type was changed from the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the new flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`). With this signature, `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` (no `teamId`) type-checks, then fails `safeParse`, sets `this.options = null`, and silently yields `1=0` — i.e. insights pages render empty data instead of surfacing a compile-time or runtime error. Keep the discriminated union as the public input type, or throw when validation fails so misuse is visible.

Public findMany() removed without updating consumers

The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment and performs no query. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (tRPC insights routers, etc.) will fail to compile/run, and no such callers are updated in this PR (only the service and its test are touched). Either keep a `findMany`-equivalent that executes the query using the new SQL conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

SQL expectations depend on unordered DB row order

The org-scope and team-scope assertions compare the generated `Prisma.Sql` (including its bound `values`) against literal arrays such as `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` and `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]`. Those arrays come from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` / `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`, which are issued without an `ORDER BY`, so Postgres may return rows in any order and the test will fail intermittently. Sort the actual/expected ID arrays before comparing, or assert on membership rather than exact array ordering.

getBaseConditions() can return an un-parenthesized OR expression

`getBaseConditions()` returns the raw SQL fragment as-is when there are no filters, and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reducers at lines 171-174 and 204-207). Any caller that composes it, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" > $x`, gets `(A AND B) OR ((C AND D) AND "startTime" > $x)` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. The first OR branch then bypasses the extra predicate entirely, which silently returns rows that should have been filtered out (a correctness and potential data-exposure problem, since the OR branches are the authorization clauses). The fragment returned by `getBaseConditions()` (and by `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()`, which are public) should always be wrapped in parentheses, e.g. `return Prisma.sql`(${conditions})``.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data to bump updatedAt

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is issued after every cache refresh with an empty `data` object, relying on Prisma implicitly setting the `@updatedAt` field. This is undocumented behavior (an empty `updateMany` can be a no-op), so the intended timestamp bump may silently never happen, while every cache refresh still pays for an extra write/row lock across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential. The PR description itself notes this value isn't consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`); either set the field explicitly (`{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or drop the call.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dev script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a CWD-relative .env path

`sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; with GNU sed (Linux/CI) the empty string is parsed as the input filename and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from the repository root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory instead of the intended file. Use a path derived from the script location and a portable in-place edit.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteCache handler throws plain Error instead of TRPCError

When the credential isn't found or doesn't belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and, depending on error formatting, can surface the raw message. This conflates an authorization/not-found condition with a server failure, breaks client error handling (which only shows a generic toast), and pollutes error monitoring with false 500s. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` as the other handlers in this router do.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone

The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see an American date/time format inside an otherwise localized string, and the user's configured timezone/time format preference (12h/24h) is ignored. Use the user's locale (available from `useLocale()`) and the existing date-formatting helpers.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as fresh

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `calendarCache` rows for the credential and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Cache rows that are already expired (and therefore never served by `getCachedAvailability`) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports a cache as present/"last updated" when there is effectively no usable cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match the read path.

Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate

The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init()` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, cache status (and therefore the "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" UI) is reported from leftover DB rows even for users/teams where calendar cache is turned off, and an extra DB groupBy runs on every connectedCalendars request regardless of the flag.

Migration header warning contradicts the statement it documents

The generated warning block states the column is "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual ALTER TABLE adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place misleads reviewers/operators into thinking the migration will fail on a non-empty CalendarCache table. Remove or correct the comment.

No tests for the new destructive deleteCache mutation or cache-status repository method

`deleteCacheHandler` performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` gated only by an ownership lookup, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new query logic, yet neither has unit tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete the cache of another user's credential (the main security property of this endpoint) nor that the credential-id-to-timestamp mapping is correct.

UserWithCalendars widened to require updatedAt/googleChannelId without need

`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in their `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` types, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. This is an exported public type consumed by other callers (platform libraries, API handlers, tests) that build the user object with only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` selected; they will now fail type-checking and must all add the two selections (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here). Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query

`deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, unlike `disconnectMutation` which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. false_positives.candidate:
One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders

The `try { for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... } }` block wraps the entire loop in a single try/catch. If the SendGrid request for one reminder throws (invalid batch_id, rate limit, transient 5xx, auth error), the loop exits immediately, the already-queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises are never awaited, and every remaining cancelled reminder in the batch is skipped for this run. Since the cron only looks at reminders scheduled within the next hour, those skipped reminders may never be retried in time and their emails will still be delivered — exactly the failure mode this PR is meant to fix. The try/catch should be per-reminder inside the loop.

Reschedule path still cancels SendGrid sends immediately, re-exposing the 100 pending-cancellation limit

That issues the `scheduled_sends` cancel straight away, and each cancellation occupies a slot in SendGrid's pending-cancellation list until the scheduled send date — which is the exact quota (max 100 pending cancellations) the PR description identifies as the root cause of reminders still being delivered. Rescheduled bookings (one of the two cases named in the PR title/issue) therefore still hit the original failure, while cancelled bookings go through the new deferred path. This should use the deferred `cancelled` flag like the cancellation path.

As a result every `client.request(...)` in this file — including the new cancellation calls — is sent unauthenticated and fails with 401; the error is swallowed by the catch, so cancellations silently never happen and the reminder emails are still sent. Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)`.

`Prisma` was moved into the value import but all of its uses (`PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>`) were removed in this diff, so the binding is now unused, and it is added without a trailing comma, which violates the repo's prettier config. Both will fail the lint/format checks in CI.

`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` awaits `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` before deleting the DB row, and the whole body is wrapped in a try/catch that only logs. If Twilio rejects the cancellation (e.g. the message already left the queue or the SID is no longer cancellable) the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` is skipped, so the row stays forever: the cron's cleanup `deleteMany` only targets `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. The query that collects reminders to cancel only filters on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`. It does not filter `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, `scheduled: true`, or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Consequences: (a) a reminder whose `referenceId` is still null (never handed to SendGrid) will produce a `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `batch_id: null`, which SendGrid rejects with a 4xx; (b) any non-EMAIL (SMS/Twilio) reminder that ever ends up with `cancelled = true` would be sent to SendGrid with a Twilio SID as batch_id. Both cases turn into request errors inside the loop, which (see the surrounding try/catch) aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders.

This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions use an async forEach and are never awaited

The external calendar events for all remaining recurring instances are therefore deleted fire-and-forget (and any failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of being reported). true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dynamic imports are invoked eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy and rejections are unhandled

The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, … at module-evaluation time. Dynamic `import()` starts loading as soon as the expression is evaluated, so every app module is still fetched and evaluated the moment `@calcom/app-store` is imported — the PR's stated goal (async/lazy loading of app packages) is not achieved, and bundlers still have to include every app in the graph. Worse, the 28 promises are created with no attached handlers at module scope: if any app module throws while being evaluated (bad env/config, side-effectful module), the resulting rejection is unhandled and can crash the Node process (unhandled rejections are fatal by default on modern Node) even when that app is never used. To get real laziness and safe error handling the values should be thunks/getters, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites doing `await appStore[key]()`.

false_positives.candidate:
Commented example import points to a non-existent path

`getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous but `getCalendar(credential)` now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`, so each returned item's `calendar` property is a promise rather than a `Calendar`. Additionally the promises are created without handlers, so if a CalendarService constructor/import rejects for a credential that is never awaited, the rejection goes unhandled. Consider making the function `async` and resolving the calendars (e.g. with `Promise.all`) before returning, so the contract stays `Calendar | null`.

requestReschedule: async callback in forEach means cancellations are not awaited

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now asynchronous, the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule-request email, fire webhooks and return while the calendar/video event deletions are still pending, and any error (e.g. expired credentials) becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. try/catch no longer protects the now-async forEach callback
