With this change the UI will offer edit/delete for federated rules, and those write operations are not supported by the ruler for federated groups, so users will hit failures (or unintentionally modify a federated group). The federated check needs to be preserved, e.g. by passing the group (or a flag) into the hook rather than stubbing it out with a TODO.

Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export/Pause/Restore abilities

In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, whereas the ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` which also matches Grafana recording rules. Since the list view now relies exclusively on this hook (ruler abilities resolve to false with no `rulerRule`), Grafana-managed recording rules can no longer be paused, exported with modifications, or restored from the rule list. If the intent was only to exclude recording rules from silencing, the alerting-only check should be limited to the `Silence` ability.

`returnTo` query param dropped from rule view link

The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` omits `returnTo`, so navigating into a rule from the list and then using the "return to previous" breadcrumb/button will no longer bring the user back to the filtered list page they came from.

Test asserts exactly 4 menu items, locking in the missing Delete action

The test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` both globally and on the folder, yet asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` and never checks `ui.menuItems.delete()` (the selector is defined but unused). This codifies the current behaviour where Delete (and Pause) are unreachable in the new list view because `AlertRuleMenu` still requires a `rulerRule` for those items. Once the menu is fixed the assertion will break; the test should explicitly assert the presence/absence of Delete and Pause so the regression is visible rather than baked in.

Stale ruler-preload naming and comment after removing the ruler prefetch

The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment ("This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded") and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` still describe ruler preloading. This is misleading for future readers who will look for ruler prefetching that no longer exists; rename/update to reflect that only the Prometheus group cache is populated.

false_negatives.golden_comment: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

false_positives.candidate:
Queries are now interpolated twice (runSplitQuery + DataSourceWithBackend.query)

`runSplitQuery` now maps every target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. The sub-requests built from these targets are executed with `datasource.runQuery(subRequest)`, which calls `super.query()` (DataSourceWithBackend.query), and that method already applies `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` to every target it sends to the backend. As a result each query is interpolated twice: `templateSrv.replace` runs over an already-substituted expression (so a variable whose value itself contains `$something`/`[[something]]` will be expanded a second time) and `addAdHocFilters` is applied a second time to an expression that already contains the ad hoc matchers, which is at best redundant LogQL parsing per sub-request and at worst produces duplicated label matchers in the selector. If interpolation must happen up front for partitioning/step calculation, the second pass should be avoided (e.g. by stripping scopedVars/filters from the sub-request or by only using the interpolated copies for partitioning decisions).

Shard path re-interpolates already sharded expressions

`runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the targets, `splitQueriesByStreamShard` then rewrites them with `interpolateShardingSelector()` (adding `__stream_shard__=~"..."` and `| drop __stream_shard__`) and hands the result to `runSplitQuery`, which (after this PR) interpolates them again, and `datasource.runQuery` interpolates a third time inside `DataSourceWithBackend.query`. So for every shard group the sharded expression is re-parsed and re-processed by `addAdHocFilters`/`templateSrv.replace` twice more. The new test assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` (shardQuerySplitting.test.ts line 112) confirms this: one interpolation became five for a single query. Besides the wasted work, re-applying ad hoc filters and variable substitution to an already-interpolated, shard-annotated expression risks duplicated matchers and double expansion of variable values that contain `$`.

New test asserts client-side interpolation of $__auto, which the real code must not do

The test mocks `templateSrv.replace` with a blind string replacement (`input.replace('$__auto', '5m')`) and then asserts that the expression reaching `runQuery` is `count_over_time({a="b"}[5m])`. In the real `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables`, `__auto`/`__interval`/`__interval_ms`/`__range*` are deliberately removed from the scoped vars so that they are interpolated on the backend with the *sub-request's* time range; a frontend interpolation of `$__auto` based on the full range would yield a wrong step/range for each split chunk. The test therefore validates behaviour that neither happens nor should happen in production and gives false confidence; it should instead cover a user-defined variable (e.g. `$step`) and explicitly assert that `$__auto` is left untouched.

Assertion hard-codes redundant interpolation count

`expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` encodes the number of times the (now repeated) interpolation happens for a single query: once in `runShardSplitQuery` plus once per shard-group sub-request via `runSplitQuery`. This number has no functional meaning, is coupled to the number of shard groups produced by the mocked label values, and will break on unrelated changes to grouping/shard-size heuristics. Prefer asserting that the interpolated expression reaches `runQuery` (or that it is called at least once per target) instead of an exact call count that documents the redundant interpolation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert is not atomic, so the device limit can be exceeded

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` reads the device count with `CountDevices` and then performs the upsert in a separate session. Concurrent anonymous requests (and multiple Grafana instances sharing a DB) can all observe a count below `deviceLimit` and then each insert a new row, so the number of anon devices can exceed the configured limit by the number of concurrent requests. If the limit is meant as a hard cap (e.g. for licensing/billing), this check needs to be done inside a transaction or enforced by a conditional insert.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same count-then-insert race: concurrent requests can pass the device count check and create devices beyond the limit. Both suggest atomic enforcement through a transaction or similar mechanism.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached when the UPDATE matched but changed nothing

`updateDevice` maps `rowsAffected == 0` to `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. On MySQL, `RowsAffected` for an UPDATE returns the number of *changed* rows, not matched rows (unless CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS is set). Since MySQL DATETIME columns have second precision, an existing, known device that re-tags within the same second with the same client IP and user agent produces 0 changed rows and will be wrongly rejected with "device limit reached", denying anonymous access to a device that is already counted. The condition conflates "row not found" with "nothing changed".
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the incorrect mapping of rowsAffected == 0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached in updateDevice. The candidate describes an additional MySQL-specific reason for zero affected rows, but flags the same erroneous assumption that zero rows indicates a device limit was reached.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache entry is written before the DB write, letting devices bypass the limit

In `tagDeviceUI` the cache key is stored (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`) before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. Now that `TagDevice` propagates the store error (impl.go:147) and `Anonymous.Authenticate` rejects the request on `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the first request from an over-limit device fails, but the cache entry is already present. Every subsequent request from the same device within the 29-minute cache TTL short-circuits at the cache check and returns nil, so the device is authenticated anonymously and never recorded. The configured device limit is therefore trivially bypassed by retrying the request, and transient DB errors are also "cached" as success.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same cache-ordering bug in tagDeviceUI: the device ID is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, so ErrDeviceLimitReached leaves a cache entry that lets retries bypass the device limit for the 29-minute TTL.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw error returned from Authenticate yields an opaque 5xx instead of a proper status/message

`Anonymous.Authenticate` returns `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which is a plain `fmt.Errorf` value. Other authn clients return `errutil`-based errors so the HTTP layer can produce a correct status code (e.g. 401/403/429) and a stable messageId. As written, a user hitting the device limit will get a generic internal-error response (and the error will be logged as an unexpected failure) rather than a meaningful "too many anonymous devices" response, making the feature hard to diagnose and inconsistent with the rest of authn.

Device tagging moved onto the synchronous auth path, adding DB round-trips per anonymous request

The previous implementation tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout; now `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` runs inline during authentication. For every cache miss (cache TTL is 29 min, and the cache is per-instance) this executes a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` plus an upsert before the request can proceed, so anonymous page loads now block on DB latency and the count scan grows with the number of stored devices. On a busy anonymous instance (or after a restart, when the cache is empty) this can noticeably increase request latency and DB load.

New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented

`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the option is not added to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or the configure-grafana documentation. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists, its default (0 = unlimited), or that reaching the limit blocks new anonymous devices from authenticating.

No test for the main intended behaviour: updating an already-known device when the limit is reached

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a *new* device is rejected once the limit is reached. The core of the feature — that an existing device (one already counted) can still be refreshed via `updateDevice` and does not get `ErrDeviceLimitReached` — is untested, as is the behaviour for a device whose row exists but is older than `anonymousDeviceExpiration`. Given the `rowsAffected == 0` heuristic used in `updateDevice`, regressions here would silently lock out already-counted anonymous users.

args slice is mutated inside the session callback, corrupting the query on retry

Inside `updateDevice` the closure does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`, mutating the captured outer `args` variable. `WithDbSession` can invoke the callback more than once (e.g. sqlite "database is locked" retries); on a second invocation the query string would be prepended again, producing `Exec(query, query, ...)` and a malformed statement/argument mismatch. Build the exec argument slice as a new local variable instead of reassigning the captured one.

anonymousDeviceLimit field is typed as `undefined`, not `number | undefined`

`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no type annotation, so TypeScript infers the field type as `undefined`. The backend always sends a numeric `anonymousDeviceLimit` (no `omitempty` on the DTO), and the value is injected via `merge(this, defaults, options)` which bypasses type checking. Consumers reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` will see the type `undefined` and cannot compare it to a number without a cast. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` to match `GrafanaConfig`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX

`ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes and reads `@loaded_locales` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two threads can both observe nil and each install a fresh array, so a locale recorded as loaded by one thread can be dropped, and `include?` can be executed concurrently with `<<`/reassignment. On non-GVL runtimes this can corrupt the array or cause repeated/missed loads. Initialize `@loaded_locales` eagerly at patch load time or perform the check inside the mutex.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same issue: @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and accessed by concurrent threads without synchronization. Its discussion of LOAD_MUTEX and potential races adds detail to the golden concern.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere

The on-demand locale loader in `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (line 68). The newly added fallback chain is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers/user notifications, rake tasks, rails console, middleware that runs before/without the before_filter — will have only the primary locale's YAML loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up the fallback locales (site default locale and `:en`) in an empty translation store and still produce a missing translation. The fallback feature therefore works inconsistently depending on the execution context. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (i.e. whenever a locale is activated) rather than only in the controller filter.

Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain (stale/cross-site translations)

The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is computed per request in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`. Two consequences: (1) after an admin changes `default_locale`, previously cached fallback results for other locales remain in the process-level LRU cache and keep returning values resolved through the old fallback locale until a reload; (2) in a multisite deployment the LRU cache is shared across all sites in the process while `SiteSetting.default_locale` is per-site, so a string resolved through site A's fallback locale can be served to site B for the same locale/key. The cache key needs to include the fallback chain (or the current site/default locale), or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise, and `.uniq.compact` ordering is wrong

`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` unguarded. If the setting is nil/not yet available (e.g. during asset precompilation, early boot, or before migrations create the site_settings table) this raises `NoMethodError`/DB errors from inside every `I18n.translate` call, since `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` invokes `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each lookup. Also, `compact` is applied after `uniq`, so a nil `locale` argument is only removed after being compared — the intent (drop nils, then dedupe) would be `.compact.uniq`. Guard the setting lookup (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`) and reorder.

FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes on every lookup, defeating Hash memoization

`I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation lookup. Unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which memoizes computed chains in the Hash, this override ignores the Hash storage and rebuilds a new array (plus a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a `to_sym`) on each call. On a hot path such as rendering a page with many translations this adds an allocation and a site-setting lookup per translation; consider caching per locale (and invalidating when `default_locale` changes).

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes a FallbackLocaleList and will 500 if fallbacks are replaced

`ensure_loaded!` is defined only on the custom `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. If anything else assigns `I18n.fallbacks` (a plugin, or `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` still present in an environment file such as development.rb/test.rb or a deployment's own copy of production.rb, which installs a plain `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`), this before_filter raises `NoMethodError` on every single request, taking the whole site down. Either define the loading helper in a place that does not depend on the fallbacks object type (e.g. in the translate accelerator, loading `I18n.fallbacks[I18n.locale]`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

No tests for the new fallback behaviour

This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), moves pluralization setup, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, yet no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves from `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then `:en`, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` dedupes, or that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locale files. Given that fallbacks are now active in all environments (the per-environment `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed), regressions here would silently change every missing-translation lookup, including in the test suite where missing translations will now be masked by the :en fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID when used without the contextual logger middleware

The explicit log params (`pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `traceID`) were removed and the middleware now relies entirely on contextual attributes injected by the separate, exported `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` plus a registered contextual log provider for the trace ID. There is no compile-time or runtime guarantee of that coupling: `NewLoggerMiddleware` is exported and any stack that omits the contextual logger middleware, or places it after the logger middleware, will produce "Plugin Request Completed" lines with no plugin/datasource/user identification at all — an operationally significant log regression that will not be caught by tests. Also note the trace ID previously came from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` (unsampled spans included); it now depends on whatever the registered contextual log provider does, so the field can disappear for unsampled traces. Either keep the identifying fields in the middleware or document/enforce the ordering dependency and add a test asserting the fields are present in the final log line.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the removal of explicit traceID extraction from LoggerMiddleware and the resulting risk of missing traceID in plugin request logs. Although it broadens the concern to other fields and contextual-provider dependencies, it includes the same underlying trace logging regression described by the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so log assertions no longer observe records

`TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now emits its log line via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so every record is written into a throwaway `TestLogger` that the test holds no reference to. Any test that injects a `plog.TestLogger` into the middleware and then asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will see zero calls, meaning the assertions either fail or (if written as "no error") silently stop verifying anything. `FromContext` (and arguably `New`) should return the same instance (or at least share the `Logs` state) so captured logs remain observable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() rather than the receiver, causing logs to be captured on an unreferenced instance and breaking assertions against the original logger.

false_positives.candidate:
Adding FromContext to the exported plugins log.Logger interface is a breaking change

`log.Logger` in `pkg/plugins/log` is an exported interface consumed across the plugin packages (and by downstream/enterprise code). Adding the `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` method means every existing implementation outside this repository (or in a repo that vendors it, e.g. grafana-enterprise fakes/wrappers) fails to compile until updated. If the intent is only to let middleware derive a contextual logger, consider a narrower optional interface (type-asserted at the call site) instead of widening the shared interface.

New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests

`contextual_logger_middleware.go` is new behaviour that the logger middleware now depends on (it is the only source of `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` in plugin request logs), yet no test file was added. true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!(...)` is called before validation runs. If `host` is nil — which happens whenever the admin endpoint is posted without a host value (`host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` can assign nil) — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback calls sub! on a nil host, causing NoMethodError instead of a validation error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown id

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil when the id does not exist (stale admin tab, double-delete, guessed id). `host.destroy` on line 16 and `save_host(nil)` from `update` then raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 instead of a 404/error JSON. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response (or `find`, which raises RecordNotFound and is handled).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify missing existence checks in update and destroy: querying an unknown EmbeddableHost ID returns nil, causing NoMethodError when passed to save_host or used to call destroy.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host comparison lowercases the column but not the incoming value

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased column against the raw value extracted from the referer. `URI#host` preserves the case the browser sent (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`), so a referer with any uppercase characters will not match a stored host and the embed request will be rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The parameter must be downcased (`host.downcase`).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same case-normalization bug: lower(host) is compared against an incoming referer host that is not downcased, causing mixed-case hosts to fail to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts keep their scheme/path, so embedding silently breaks after upgrade

Existing values of the `embeddable_hosts` setting could contain entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old spec and docs explicitly supported this). The migration inserts those raw strings directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` callback that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value with `URI(referer).host`, which never contains a scheme or path, so every migrated row with a scheme/path will stop matching and embedding will start returning `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme and path) before inserting.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: raw SQL migration bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization, preserving schemes or paths in stored hosts and causing bare-host lookups to fail for existing embedding configurations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents are swapped

`spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this makes the fabricators impossible to locate by filename and will confuse every future change to either model's fixtures.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same underlying issue: the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb were swapped, placing fabricator definitions in the wrong files. The differing descriptions of consequences do not change the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped string interpolation into INSERT statement

The host value from the old site setting is interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any value containing a single quote (or stray whitespace/CR from splitting on "\n" only) will produce invalid SQL and abort the migration; it is also an injection vector from stored data. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert, and strip each entry.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify direct SQL interpolation of the host value ('#{h}') as an SQL injection vulnerability and recommend parameter binding or proper quoting. The candidate's additional migration and whitespace concerns do not change the underlying match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration raises NoMethodError when `embed_category` site setting row is absent

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings are only persisted when changed from their default, so on the vast majority of installs there is no `embed_category` row (and even when there is, the join on category *name* may not match). `PG::Result#[]` returns nil for a missing row, so `[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`, aborting the migration and leaving the deployment half-migrated. false_positives.candidate:
`create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and its data

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If this migration is ever re-run (or a table of that name already exists, e.g. created by a plugin or a partially applied deploy) all existing rows are silently destroyed. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

Hosts with a port pass validation but can never match a referer

The validation regex permits an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port and the `before_validation` callback only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:3000` is stored as-is. However `record_for_host` matches against `URI(referer).host`, which never includes the port, so any host saved with a port will never be allowed and embedding from that origin always fails. Either strip the port on save or compare against host+port.

Host format regex rejects valid hosts that previously worked

`\.[a-z]{2,5}` restricts the TLD to 2–5 characters and requires at least one dot, so hosts such as `blog.technology`, `foo.website`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or an intranet hostname are rejected. The replaced `embeddable_hosts` site setting (a `host_list`) accepted these, so admins migrating from it cannot re-add such hosts through the new UI.

No uniqueness validation or index on host

Nothing prevents two rows with the same host (possibly pointing at different categories), which makes `record_for_host`'s `.first` result arbitrary and therefore the category used for new embedded topics non-deterministic. There is also no index on `host`, while `host_allowed?` runs on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?`, which cannot use a plain index. Consider a uniqueness validation plus a unique index on `lower(host)`.

Missing `embeddable_host` params cause a 500

`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises `NoMethodError` if the `embeddable_host` key is absent from the request. The controller should require the parameter (e.g. `params.require(:embeddable_host)`) so a malformed request yields a 400 rather than an exception.

The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and does not put an `embeddable_hosts` array in the JSON root. The client's `_hydrateEmbedded` resolves `*_ids` by looking up `root['embeddable_hosts']`; when that collection is missing, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for every id, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. `embed: :ids, include: true` (side-loading) is required.

`embedding#update` is a no-op that reports success

The `update` action persists nothing — it only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will report success without any change having been made. Either implement the update or remove the route, action and the unused client-side `saveChanges`.

In the new `*_ids` branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if the serialized value is `null` rather than an array, and `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` can never fall back to `[]` because `hydrated` is always an array — if the side-loaded collection is missing, the result is an array of `undefined` values while the original `*_ids` key is unconditionally deleted, so the data is lost rather than left intact. The singular branch correctly only deletes the key when a lookup succeeded; the plural branch should behave the same and guard against non-array values.

`type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore

`String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so a type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_admin_model`) will never match an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS` and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`).

No tests for the new embeddable host CRUD endpoints

The only assertion is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. The new `create`, `update` and `destroy` actions control the embedding whitelist (a security boundary: which external sites may embed the forum) and contain non-trivial logic (category fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, nil-record handling, error rendering), none of which is exercised. At minimum add tests that a host can be created/updated/deleted, that validation errors are returned, and that a non-admin is refused.

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer looks at embeddable hosts at all. This example passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic, so the name is misleading and the assertion no longer covers anything related to hosts. Rename or remove it.

Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

`include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it is never used

ActiveModel::Serializers only consults predicate methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — e.g. it is emitted as `"website_name": null` for every user with no website, and, more importantly, it bypasses the intended guard entirely. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and ideally base it on `website_name.present?`).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same primary issue: the missing '?' suffix on include_website_name prevents the serializer's conditional inclusion predicate from being recognized. It does not mention the golden comment's additional string-literal mutation concern, but directly matches the main bug.

`website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking TL0 websites to anonymous users

`:website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous visitors (anti-spam / SEO protection). The new `:website_name` attribute was added to `attributes` but not to `untrusted_attributes` and has no working inclusion guard, so the host (and now even the full path) of a TL0 user's website is serialized for anonymous requests, and `user.hbs` renders it (`{{#if model.website_name}}`). This re-exposes exactly the spam vector the untrusted_attributes list exists to block. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

TL0/anonymous spec not updated for the new `website_name` attribute

The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only contains `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not asserted to be absent, which is why the regression that leaks a TL0 user's website host/path to anonymous visitors is not caught. Add `website_name` to that list (and a case asserting `website_name` is omitted when the profile website is blank).

`"" << website_host` mutates a string literal instead of concatenating

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment the file gets a `# frozen_string_literal: true` magic comment (or runs under `--enable-frozen-string-literal`), breaking user serialization site-wide. Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

Same-suffix heuristic treats unrelated hosts on shared domains as the same site

The second branch considers two hosts related whenever they have the same number of labels (>2) and match after dropping the first label. For shared hosting suffixes this is wrong: with an instance on `forum.github.io`, an arbitrary user website `spammer.github.io` is judged to belong to the same organisation and the full URL path is rendered instead of only the host. Since the whole purpose of showing only the host is to avoid displaying attacker-controlled path text, this heuristic should use a public-suffix check or be restricted to an exact/parent-domain match.

Only `path` is appended; query/fragment are dropped and `URI()` is re-parsed repeatedly

`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` drops any query string or fragment, so `http://example.com/u?id=1` is displayed as `example.com/u`, which does not match the href the user clicks. It also re-parses the URI on every branch (up to twice per call) outside the `rescue nil` guard of line 138. Parse once into a local variable and build the display string from `path`, `query` and `fragment`.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked`

`cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline and the `after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `i.content` from an arbitrary remote RSS/Atom feed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with this cook method, so anything the feed publisher puts in the item body (`<script>`, event handlers, iframes) is rendered verbatim to every forum visitor — a stored XSS vector. The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. If the process dies or the Redis connection fails between the two calls, the throttle key exists with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, so that embed URL can never be imported again (the embed page will loop on the loading template indefinitely). Use `SET key 1 EX 60 NX` (or `setex` guarded by existence) instead.

This migration was already shipped; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that on any database where the migration is re-run (re-seeded schema, repaired schema_migrations, `db:migrate:redo`) the existing `top_topics` table is dropped along with its data instead of failing loudly. When a `TopicEmbed` row already exists, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post hard-deleted or the association pointing at a missing row). The code then calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising NoMethodError inside the retrieval job/feed poll. Guard on `post.blank?` and either recreate the topic or skip.

`import` mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the argument supplied by the caller rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or cache the content (and any frozen string passed in, which would raise) get surprising behaviour, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate multiple "Imported from" footers. `feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:` Redis key but nothing in the class (or anywhere else in the PR) reads or writes it, so there is no conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since handling as the name implies. Either implement the caching it was intended for or remove the method so future readers don't assume polling is throttled.

`discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads after 30s. The browser/proxy will serve the cached loading page for the first reload, so the user waits at least a minute even when the topic was imported quickly. `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` sets a non-standard token. Browsers that don't recognise it are entitled to fall back to denying framing, which would break embedding entirely. The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's settled/success handler.

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `calendarCache` rows for the credential and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Cache rows that are already expired (and therefore never served by `getCachedAvailability`) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports a cache as present/"last updated" when there is effectively no usable cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match the read path.

UserWithCalendars widened to require updatedAt/googleChannelId without need

`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in their `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` types, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. This is an exported public type consumed by other callers (platform libraries, API handlers, tests) that build the user object with only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` selected; they will now fail type-checking and must all add the two selections (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here). Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type

The `data` parameter is typed `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, but `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. `UpdateInput` permits nested relation writes (e.g. `credential: { connect: ... }`) which `updateMany` cannot execute, so such a call type-checks but fails at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate

The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init()` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, cache status (and therefore the "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" UI) is reported from leftover DB rows even for users/teams where calendar cache is turned off, and an extra DB groupBy runs on every connectedCalendars request regardless of the flag.

No tests for the new destructive deleteCache mutation or cache-status repository method

`deleteCacheHandler` performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` gated only by an ownership lookup, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new query logic, yet neither has unit tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete the cache of another user's credential (the main security property of this endpoint) nor that the credential-id-to-timestamp mapping is correct.

dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency

`dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` but `tsx` is not listed in this package's dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt to download it from the network on every run (failing in offline/locked-down environments and ignoring the yarn lockfile), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the local binary.

Migration header warning contradicts the statement it documents

The generated warning block states the column is "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual ALTER TABLE adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place misleads reviewers/operators into thinking the migration will fail on a non-empty CalendarCache table. Remove or correct the comment.

As a result the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never considers the event length, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them is not detected by this check.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that the end time is incorrectly calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:

`if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs objects by reference, which is never true. The intended check (a zero-length override, i.e. the organizer marked the day unavailable) therefore never executes. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: === compares distinct Dayjs object references rather than date values, making the condition always false. Both recommend .isSame() to compare the values.

false_positives.candidate:
Date-override days bypass the busy-time check entirely

In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override block, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns early, before `busy.every(...)` is evaluated. This means that for any slot on a day that has a date override, existing Cal bookings and external-calendar busy times for that host are completely ignored, so already-booked slots are reported as available. Since every non-round-robin host is treated as `isFixed`, this applies to personal and collective events too, and leads to double bookings on any day with a date override. The override result must be combined with the busy check instead of short-circuiting it.

Working-hours check rejects slots when a host has multiple availability windows on the same day

The new check uses `workingHours.find((workingHour) => { ... if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true; })` and treats a truthy result as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. `getUserAvailability` returns one working-hours entry per availability row, so a user with a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same weekday) has two entries for that day. A 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so `find` matches the second entry and the slot is dropped. The logic must be `!workingHours.some(entry => slot is inside entry)` (i.e. unavailable only if no entry contains the slot). As written, availability is silently broken for every user with more than one availability window per day.

Date-override check rejects slots when a host has several ranges on the same date

`dateOverrides.find((date) => { ... })` returns truthy as soon as *one* override range on the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the code then returns `false` ("slot is not within the date override"). A date override may legitimately contain multiple time ranges for the same date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00). A slot inside the first range is outside the second, so it is incorrectly marked unavailable. The predicate must be inverted to "no range on that date contains the slot".

Override date compared in server-local time against a UTC slot time

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the process's local timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`time.utc()`). On a deployment whose system timezone is not UTC, the two date strings can differ for the same instant, so overrides are matched to the wrong day (or not matched at all), making the whole override branch behave differently per server timezone. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for the comparison.

Override end check ignores event length, allowing bookings that overrun the override

`if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")))` only tests the slot's *start* against the override end. For an override of 14:00-15:00 and a 60-minute event, a slot starting at 14:30 ends at 15:30 but is still considered inside the override and returned as available. Since for fixed hosts in round-robin events this is the only check against that host's override window, the fixed host can be booked outside their declared override. The comparison should use `slotEndTime`.

Override timeZone is optional; dayjs .tz(undefined) silently falls back to the default timezone

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `override.timeZone` typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts). Any caller of `getSlots` that passes date overrides without a `timeZone` (the field is newly added, so existing callers do not set it) will have `.tz(undefined)` resolve to dayjs's default/guessed timezone, producing a wrong `organizerUtcOffset` and shifting the override by an arbitrary amount. Either make the field required on this code path or explicitly fall back to a known timezone (e.g. UTC) when it is missing.

Timezone-shifted override wraps around midnight and lands on the wrong day

`startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour() * 60 + minute()` of the offset-shifted override time, i.e. minutes since the invitee's midnight. When the shift pushes the override across a day boundary the day information is lost: e.g. an organizer override 09:00-11:00 in UTC+5:30 viewed by an invitee in UTC-8 shifts to 19:30-21:30 of the *previous* day, but is emitted as minutes 1170-1290 of the invitee's current day, so slots are offered at a completely wrong time. Negative/over-1440 minute offsets need to be handled (clip to the day or split across days), as `buildSlots` only understands minutes within the invitee day.

No test for the PR's main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)

The PR's primary change is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (via the new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` handling in `checkIfIsAvailable`), but the only test added covers invitee-timezone handling for a single personal event. There is no test with a round-robin event type where a fixed host has a date override and the round-robin host does not, which is exactly the regression-prone path (and the path where the `dateOverrideExist -> return true` short-circuit and the split-working-hours bug manifest). Please add a getSchedule test for that scenario, including a host with multiple availability windows on the override day.

toHaveTimeSlots matcher cannot detect missing slots

The matcher iterates with `.every()` over the *actual* slots and compares them index-wise to `expectedSlots`, without comparing array lengths. If the implementation returns fewer slots than expected (e.g. the first N are correct but trailing slots are dropped), the assertion still passes. The newly added timezone assertion relies on this matcher, so a partial regression in override handling would go unnoticed; the matcher should also assert `schedule.slots[dateString].length === expectedSlots.length`.

`getBaseConditions()` returns the raw SQL fragment as-is when there are no filters, and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reducers at lines 171-174 and 204-207). The first OR branch then bypasses the extra predicate entirely, which silently returns rows that should have been filtered out (a correctness and potential data-exposure problem, since the OR branches are the authorization clauses). true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string `"[object Object]"` (Zod types have no `toString` override), so the object literal ends up with a single extra key literally named `"[object Object]"`, with the second definition overwriting the first. The candidate explains their unintended schema behavior rather than the runtime error described by the golden comment, but targets the same problematic code and misuse of Zod.

true_positives.matched_candidate: Anchor verification is order-sensitive and mutates the string it is iterating `santizeAnchors` pairs the n-th anchor tag of the translation with the n-th anchor tag of the English source and requires exact equality. A translation that legitimately reorders two links (English `... .. ... ..`, translation with the links swapped) is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" even though it contains exactly the same tags, i.e. a false build failure. In addition, `value` is reassigned inside the loop while `matcher` keeps iterating the original snapshot, and the removal is done with `replaceFirst` on the *English* group, so the occurrence that is removed is not necessarily the one just matched. Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next resource bundle

This bundle is consumed by the account console through i18next, where placeholders must be written as `{{0}}` (see every other entry in this file, e.g. `error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character.`). The Java MessageFormat form is only correct for the server-side `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/**` bundles.

`verifySafeHtml()` derives the English bundle path by string replacement and then opens it unconditionally; if the file does not exist (community-only theme/message directory with no `messages_en.properties` under `resources`, a bundle without a locale suffix where the regex does not match, or a newly added community locale) a `FileNotFoundException` is wrapped into a plain `RuntimeException`. Anchor failure message does not say which key or file is affected

The message added here is only "Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string", while all other messages produced by this class include the key and the file name. With hundreds of message bundles being verified, a build failure with this text gives the contributor no way to locate the offending entry. Properties are read as ISO-8859-1 while Keycloak theme bundles are UTF-8

`new PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` is specified to decode the stream as ISO-8859-1. The consequence is that the "Illegal HTML in key ... : '<x>' vs '<y>'" diagnostics printed for those locales are garbled and hard to act on, and any future check that depends on the real characters would be wrong. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))` (same for the English bundle) to match how the files are actually encoded.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong characters and inverts the comparison

The new matcher is supposed to assert that the event's TOKEN_ID encodes the expected grant shortcut. The encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 for session type, 2 for token type, 2 for grant type), so the grant shortcut lives at indexes 4..6, but the code reads `items[0].substring(3, 5)` (e.g. for "onrtac" it extracts "ta" instead of "ac"). In addition the condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the grant shortcut *does* match and passes when it does not. The net effect is that all the converted assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) silently validate nothing about the grant encoding, so a regression in the encoding would go unnoticed; and if the extracted substring ever happens to equal the expected shortcut the tests would fail for a correct token.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug in isAccessTokenId: the grant shortcut is read from the wrong character range and the equality check is inverted so a matching shortcut returns false. The candidate's index phrasing differs slightly but points to the same underlying defect and consequence.

false_positives.candidate:
New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations

`getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Any existing third-party/deployed grant type factory that does not implement it will no longer compile, and pre-compiled providers will throw `AbstractMethodError` at server startup, because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` invokes `getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory. Providing a `default` implementation (e.g. returning null / a derived value) and handling the null case in the encoder would avoid breaking existing extensions.

Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed

The copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` is deleted from the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in server-spi-private. Custom grant type implementations (or any code outside this repository) that create a derived context by copying an existing one will fail to compile / throw NoSuchMethodError after upgrade. If the removal is intentional it should at least be called out as a breaking SPI change; otherwise keep it and copy the new `grantType` field as well.

Lazy grant/shortcut registration bypasses the duplicate-shortcut validation

`getShortcutByGrantType()` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` lazily add entries to `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` without re-running the duplicate detection performed in `postInit()`. If a grant type registered later (e.g. a dynamically deployed provider) reuses an existing shortcut, the mapping is silently overwritten, so `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will decode previously issued tokens to the wrong grant type. The duplicate check should also be applied on the lazy path (or the collision logged/rejected).

Session type derived from clientSession.getUserSession() instead of the user session already available

`getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` dereferences `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` without a null check. `TokenManager.initToken` already has the authoritative `UserSessionModel` as a parameter but does not pass it; for client sessions that are not (yet) attached to a user session this will NPE while building the access token, turning a token request into a 500. Passing the user session explicitly (or null-guarding and falling back to SessionType.UNKNOWN) would be safer.

Access token jti format change is not documented / no upgrade note

Access token ids (`jti`, and the `token_id` event detail) change from a plain UUID to `<6-char context>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`). This is an externally visible format change: clients, log pipelines or custom extensions that assume `jti` is a UUID (or that it contains no ':' character, e.g. when used in URLs or as a cache key) will break. The PR contains no documentation or upgrade/release note describing the new format and its stability guarantees.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
removeStoredCredentialById() is called with a federated credential id

After the lookup was switched to `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, the credential returned here may come from the user storage (federated) instead of the local credential store. The code then calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`, which only operates on the local store, so for a federated credential the call silently does nothing (and the id may even be null, as it is for the testsuite provider which rebuilds the model with `createFromValues`). Consequence: when a federated provider reports all codes as used, the exhausted credential is never removed and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action will be re-added on every subsequent login, leaving the user in a loop. The removal/reset needs to be delegated to the user storage (e.g. via disableCredentialType/updateCredential) when the credential is federated.

false_positives.candidate:
New, undocumented user-storage contract: all raw recovery codes passed as a JSON array in the credential value

createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the full list of *raw* (unhashed) recovery codes into a JSON array and passes it as the challenge-response/value of a UserCredentialModel of type `recovery-authn-codes` to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`. This establishes a brand new, completely undocumented contract that every UserStorageProvider must now implement to receive recovery codes (the JSON encoding, the fact that the value is a list and not a single code, that the provider is responsible for hashing them and for invalidating individual codes after use). Nothing in the SPI javadoc, the UserStorage documentation, or a migration note describes it; the only example is the testsuite provider, which stores the codes in clear text and compares them with `String.equals`. Without documentation, third-party providers will either reject the update (silently falling back to local storage) or mis-store the codes. At minimum the method javadoc should specify the wire format and the provider's obligations (hashing, single-use invalidation).

Federated-first credential lookup can disagree with credential validation order and with an existing local credential

getCredential() returns the federated recovery-codes credential if the user storage exposes one, and only otherwise the locally stored one. A user can legitimately have both (e.g. codes were created locally before the federation provider started supporting the type, or a previous `updateCredential` returned false). In that case the login form renders the "next code number" taken from the federated model while `credentialManager().isValid()` may validate against the other credential, so the user is asked for code N but only code M is accepted, making login impossible. The helper should either take the credential from the same source that will validate it, or the creation path should delete the stale local credential when the credential is stored in the user storage.

getCredentials() dereferences a possibly null MyUser

`var myUser = getMyUser(user);` can return null (getMyUser is a plain map lookup by username, and every other method in this class — isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isValid — explicitly null-checks it). `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 then throws NullPointerException whenever getCredentials is invoked for a user that is no longer in the in-memory map (e.g. after removeUser, or for a stale cached UserModel), which will surface as a 500 in account/admin endpoints that list credentials and make tests flaky. Add the null check and return Stream.empty().

Federated recovery-codes credential is rebuilt on every call, losing id and used-code state

getCredentials() builds a fresh `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)` from the raw codes on each invocation. The returned model therefore has no id and always reports every code as unused, and the provider never marks a code as consumed in isValid(). As a result this reference provider models recovery codes as infinitely reusable, the credential cannot be addressed by id (account console delete, removeStoredCredentialById), and the new test cannot detect a regression in the single-use semantics of recovery codes.

New test only covers one successful login; no coverage of code consumption, wrong code, or fallback to local storage

testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only sets up codes and performs a single successful login with code #0. It does not verify that the used code is rejected on a second login / that the form then asks for the next code, does not verify that an invalid code is rejected, does not assert that no credential leaked into the local DB *after* the login, and does not cover the other branch of the new code in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (a federated user whose storage does not support `recovery-authn-codes`, which must fall back to the local credential store). The two behaviours this PR is about — storing in user storage and falling back to local — are therefore only half covered.

Unneeded 'delayed-authenticator' execution (with typo'd config alias) added to the test browser flow

configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes adds a REQUIRED `delayed-authenticator` execution with delay 0 and a config alias typo ("delayed-suthenticator-config"). The delay serves no purpose for this test, but it makes the flow (and the test) depend on an extra testsuite authenticator being deployed and on the `delay` config being accepted; if that provider is unavailable the flow fails at authentication time for reasons unrelated to recovery codes. The parameter and the execution should be dropped (or at least the alias typo fixed).

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removing the BuildIndex-wide lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index

Previously `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for its whole duration, which made a concurrent `GetIndex` (RLock) block until the build finished, so a second caller observed the finished index instead of starting its own build. Now the lock is only taken around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write, so two callers (e.g. the startup indexing goroutines in `searchSupport.init` and a watch event going through `getOrCreateIndex`) can both see `GetIndex == nil` for the same NamespacedResource and build in parallel. For file-based indexes this means two goroutines call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory (`Root/namespace/resource.group`), and the second one fails (path already exists) or corrupts the on-disk index; for memory indexes the work is duplicated and one index is silently dropped from the cache while documents may still be written to it. The duplicate-build window needs to be guarded per key (e.g. keyed mutex / singleflight) rather than removed entirely.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race caused by narrowing cacheMu protection in BuildIndex, allowing multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same index for one key.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu

`TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` now writes to that map from many concurrent goroutines (the lock was narrowed to just the map write). Concurrent map read + write causes a fatal `concurrent map read and map write` runtime panic. This path is newly exercised on every startup by the added log line in `searchSupport.init` (`s.search.TotalDocs()`), and can also be hit at any time if metrics/logging call it while a watch event triggers a lazy index build. `TotalDocs` should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache unsynchronized while concurrent BuildIndex writes (triggered by the event watcher / startup log call) can cause a concurrent map read/write panic.

false_positives.candidate:
init() goroutines write shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization

Inside `group.Go(...)` the closures do `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)`, both of which mutate variables declared in the enclosing function from up to `initWorkers` goroutines running in parallel. This is a data race (detectable by `-race`, and the counter reported in the `namespaces indexed` span event can be wrong/undercounted), and assigning to the shared `err` instead of returning the value through the errgroup can also overwrite an error from another worker. Use a local `err :=` inside the closure (returning it) and an atomic counter.

Stop()'s initErr is no longer surfaced; requests are served after shutdown

All the per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return ... }` guards were removed, but `Stop()` still communicates shutdown exclusively by setting `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`. Since nothing reads `initErr` after construction anymore, calls arriving during or after shutdown no longer fail fast; they proceed against a backend whose lifecycle hooks have been stopped and whose watcher context has been cancelled, producing confusing internal errors instead of a clear "service is stopping" response. Either add an explicit closed/stopped check on the request paths or drop the now-dead initErr mutation in Stop().

Context cancel func leaked when Init fails in NewResourceServer

`ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created a few lines above, and on the new `s.Init(ctx)` error path the function returns `nil, err` without ever calling `cancel()`. The cancel func is also only reachable through the discarded `server` value, so the derived context (and any timer/goroutine attached to it) is leaked for the lifetime of the process. Call `cancel()` before returning the error (also applies to the `newSearchSupport` error return just above).

Index build now blocks server construction and makes startup fail hard

`NewResourceServer` now runs the full `Init` (lifecycle init + building every namespace's search index) synchronously before returning. Two consequences worth confirming: (1) process/DI startup is blocked for as long as indexing takes (the PR description says it can exceed a gRPC deadline, i.e. potentially minutes on large installs), so nothing else that depends on this constructor — including the HTTP server/readiness endpoint in single-binary mode — comes up during that time; (2) any transient failure during index build (DB hiccup, bleve directory error) now aborts construction and prevents the server from starting at all, whereas before only the failing request errored and a later request would retry `Init`. Consider doing the index build in the background with a readiness gate, or at least bounding it with a timeout and tolerating per-namespace failures.

BuildIndex still discards the span context, breaking the trace fix for builder work

The PR fixes trace propagation in `searchSupport.build` and `GetResourceStats` by assigning the derived context, but `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`. The builder callback invoked at line 126 uses the context captured from `searchSupport.build`, so all storage/list spans produced during the actual index build are siblings of the `BuildIndex` span rather than children, and the BuildIndex span appears empty in traces. Propagate the derived context into `builder(idx)` (e.g. by making the builder accept a ctx or by assigning `ctx, span := ...`).

Given this PR changes when unified storage initializes (now inside `NewResourceServer`, i.e. during module startup), postgres is exactly the configuration where a startup regression would go unnoticed. The skip reason ("works locally") suggests the test is actually failing with these changes in CI; the root cause should be understood before merging, and the TODO should reference a tracking issue so the coverage is restored.
